title.zh: 卷127 志一百二 河渠二 运河
title.en: Volume 127 Treatises 102: Rivers and Canals 2, Yun He
title.raw: 卷127 志一百二 河渠二 运河

sentences.zh: 志一百二

translations.literal: Treatise one hundred and two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 102.

sentences.zh: 運河自京師歷直沽、山東，下達揚子江口，南北二千餘里，又自京口抵杭州，首尾八百餘里，通謂之運河。

translations.literal: The Grand Canal from the capital passes through Zhigu and Shandong, reaching the mouth of the Yangzi, more than two thousand li north and south; again from Jingkou to Hangzhou, head to tail more than eight hundred li—all are commonly called the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal runs from the capital through Zhigu and Shandong to the Yangzi estuary—a north–south stretch of over two thousand li—and from Jingkou to Hangzhou a further eight hundred li or so; together these waterways are known as the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 明代有白漕、衛漕、閘漕、河漕、湖漕、江漕、浙漕之別。

translations.literal: The Ming had distinctions of Bai transport, Wei transport, lock transport, river transport, lake transport, Jiang transport, and Zhe transport.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, grain transport was divided into Bai, Wei, lock, river, lake, Jiang, and Zhe routes.

sentences.zh: 清自康熙中靳輔開中河，避黃流之險，糧艘經行黃河不過數里，即入中河，於是百八十里之河漕遂廢。

translations.literal: The Qing, from the middle of the Kangxi reign when Jin Fu opened the Middle Canal, avoiding the peril of the Yellow current, grain ships passing the Yellow River did not exceed a few li before entering the Middle Canal; thus the hundred and eighty li of river transport was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi era Jin Fu cut the Middle Canal to skirt the hazards of the Yellow River: grain fleets now sailed only a few li on the Yellow River before entering the new channel, and the old hundred-and-eighty-li river transport route fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 若白漕之藉資白河，衛漕之導引衛水，閘漕、湖漕之分受山東、江南諸湖水，與明代無異。

translations.literal: As for Bai transport relying on the Bai River, Wei transport channeling Wei waters, and lock and lake transport dividing among themselves the lake waters of Shandong and Jiangnan, there was no difference from the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Bai transport still drew on the Bai River, Wei transport on the Wei River, and lock and lake transport on the lakes of Shandong and the lower Yangzi region—much as in Ming times.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶之季，河流屢決，運道被淤，因而借黃濟運。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiaqing reign, rivers repeatedly burst, the transport channel was silted, and therefore they borrowed the Yellow to aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jiaqing reign repeated breaches silted the canal, and the state again used Yellow River water to keep transport moving.

sentences.zh: 道光初，試行海運。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daoguang reign, sea transport was tried.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang reign the court experimented with shipping grain by sea.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，復因節省幫費，續運一次。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, again because of saving escort expenses, transport was continued once more.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of his reign, Daoguang ordered one more sea shipment to cut escort costs.

sentences.zh: 迨咸豐朝，黃河北徙，中原多故，運道中梗。

translations.literal: By the Xianfeng court, the Yellow River shifted north, the central plain had many troubles, and the transport channel was blocked in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianfeng the Yellow River veered north, turmoil spread across the north China plain, and the canal corridor was cut.

sentences.zh: 終清之世，海運遂以為常。

translations.literal: Through the end of the Qing age, sea transport thus became the norm.
translations.idiomatic: For the rest of the dynasty, sea transport became the regular practice.

sentences.zh: 夫黃河南行，淮先受病，淮病而運亦病。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River runs south, the Huai first suffers illness; when the Huai is ill, transport is also ill.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River turned south, the Huai bore the first damage—and a sick Huai meant a sick transport system.

sentences.zh: 由是治河、導淮、濟運三策，群萃於淮安、清口一隅，施工之勤，糜帑之鉅，人民田廬之頻歲受災，未有甚於此者。

translations.literal: Hence the three policies of regulating the river, guiding the Huai, and aiding transport all gathered in the corner of Huai'an and Qingkou; diligence of construction, vastness of treasury expenditure, and the people's fields and houses suffering disaster year after year—nothing exceeded this.
translations.idiomatic: River control, Huai regulation, and canal relief therefore converged on Huai'an and Qingkou. Nowhere else matched the relentless works, the vast outlays of silver, or the yearly ruin of farms and homes.

sentences.zh: 蓋清口一隅，意在蓄清敵黃。

translations.literal: For the corner of Qingkou, the intent was to store clear water to oppose the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingkou the aim was to hold clear water against the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 然淮強固可刷黃，而過盛則運堤莫保，淮弱末由濟運，黃流又有倒灌之虞，非若白漕、衛漕僅從事疏淤塞決，閘漕、湖漕但期蓄泄得宜而已。

translations.literal: Yet if the Huai was strong it could indeed scour the Yellow, but if excessive the transport dikes could not be preserved; if the Huai was weak there was no means to aid transport, and the Yellow current also had the worry of backflow—not like Bai and Wei transport, which only engaged in dredging silt and blocking breaches, or lock and lake transport, which only expected storage and discharge to be appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: A strong Huai could scour the Yellow, but too much water threatened the canal dikes; a weak Huai could not feed transport, while Yellow backflow remained a constant fear. Bai and Wei routes chiefly required dredging and breach repair; lock and lake routes needed only balanced storage and release—far simpler problems.

sentences.zh: 至江漕、浙漕，號稱易治。

translations.literal: As for Jiang and Zhe transport, they were called easy to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Zhe transport, by contrast, were regarded as comparatively easy to maintain.

sentences.zh: 江漕自湖廣、江西沿漢、沔、鄱陽而下，同入儀河，溯流上駛。

translations.literal: Jiang transport from Huguang and Jiangxi followed the Han, Mian, and Poyang downward, together entering the Yi River, and went upstream against the current.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang grain came down the Han, Mian, and Poyang from Huguang and Jiangxi into the Yi River, then steamed upstream.

sentences.zh: 京口以南，運河惟徒、陽、陽武等邑時勞疏濬，無錫而下，直抵蘇州，與嘉、杭之運河，固皆清流順軌，不煩人力。

translations.literal: South of Jingkou, on the canal only counties such as Tu, Yang, and Yangwu from time to time labored at dredging; from Wuxi downward, straight to Suzhou, and the canals of Jia and Hang, all were clear currents on smooth courses, not troubling human effort.
translations.idiomatic: South of Jingkou only a few counties such as Tu, Yang, and Yangwu needed periodic dredging; from Wuxi to Suzhou and on to Jiaxing and Hangzhou the water ran clear and true, with little need for labor.

sentences.zh: 今撮其受患最甚、工程最鉅者著於篇。

translations.literal: Now the sections where suffering was greatest and works were largest are gathered and set down in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: This chapter records the stretches that suffered most and demanded the heaviest works.

sentences.zh: 順治四年夏久雨，決江都運堤，隨塞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi, summer long rain, the Jiangdu transport dike burst, and was soon closed.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Shunzhi 4 prolonged rain breached the Jiangdu canal dike; it was repaired soon after.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，高郵運堤決數百丈。

translations.literal: In the sixth year summer, the Gaoyou transport dike burst for several hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year the Gaoyou canal dike gave way for several hundred zhang.

sentences.zh: 七年，運堤潰，挾汶水由鹽河入海。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the transport dike collapsed, carrying Wen waters through the salt river to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the canal dike failed and Wen River water rushed out to sea via the salt route.

sentences.zh: 八年，募民夫大挑運河。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, civilian laborers were recruited for a major dredging of the canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the government hired laborers for a large-scale canal dredging.

sentences.zh: 十四年，河督硃之錫言：「南旺南距台庄高百二十尺，北距臨清高九十尺，應遵定例，非積六七尺不準啟閘，以免瀉涸。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, River Director Zhu Zhixi said: 'South of Nanwang, south to Taizhuang is one hundred and twenty chi high; north to Linqing is ninety chi high. The fixed regulations should be followed: unless water has accumulated six or seven chi, opening the lock is not permitted, to avoid draining dry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Director-General of Rivers Zhu Zhixi reported: 'From Nanwang the fall to Taizhuang is one hundred twenty chi and to Linqing ninety. Locks must follow statute: do not open until six or seven chi have built up, lest the channel drain empty.

sentences.zh: 閉下閘，啟上閘，水凝亦深；

translations.literal: Close the lower lock, open the upper lock—even sluggish water is also deep;
translations.idiomatic: Close the lower gate and open the upper—even sluggish water runs deep;

sentences.zh: 閉上閘，啟下閘，水旺亦淺。

translations.literal: close the upper lock, open the lower lock—even surging water is also shallow.
translations.idiomatic: close the upper and open the lower—even a full current can prove shallow.

sentences.zh: 重運板不輕啟，回空板不輕閉。」

translations.literal: The heavy-laden transport boards should not be lightly opened; the empty-return boards should not be lightly closed.'
translations.idiomatic: Do not open gates lightly for northbound grain fleets, nor close them lightly for empty southbound craft.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十五年，董口淤。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Dongkou silted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Dongkou silted up.

sentences.zh: 之錫於石牌口迤南開新河二百五十丈，接連大河，以通飛輓。

translations.literal: Zhixi south of Shipai mouth opened a new river two hundred and fifty zhang, connecting to the great river, to pass swift towing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixi cut a new channel two hundred fifty zhang south of Shipai, linking it to the main stream so rapid transport could pass.

sentences.zh: 先是漳水於九年從丘縣北流，逕青縣入海。

translations.literal: Earlier the Zhang River in the ninth year flowed north from Qiu county, going straight through Qing county to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the ninth year, the Zhang River had shifted north from Qiu County and reached the sea via Qing County.

sentences.zh: 至十七年春夏之交，衛水微弱，糧運澀滯，乃堰漳河分溉民田之水，入衛濟運。

translations.literal: By the turn of spring and summer in the seventeenth year, Wei waters were feeble, grain transport was sluggish and delayed, and therefore they dammed the Zhang River water divided to irrigate civilian fields, bringing it into the Wei to aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year weak Wei flow stalled grain transport; officials dammed Zhang River water that had been split for irrigation and diverted it into the Wei to feed the canal.

sentences.zh: 時河北累年亢旱，部司姜天樞言：「昔僉事江良材欲導河注衛，增一運道，今獨不可借其議而反用之導衛以注河乎？」

translations.literal: At the time Hebei for successive years had severe drought. Department official Jiang Tian'ai said: 'Formerly Vice Commissioner Jiang Liangcai wished to guide the river to pour into the Wei, adding one transport route—now alone cannot we borrow his proposal and instead use it in reverse, guiding the Wei to pour into the river?'
translations.idiomatic: Hebei had suffered drought for years. Board official Jiang Tian'ai argued: 'Former Vice Commissioner Jiang Liangcai once proposed diverting the river into the Wei to open another transport line—why not reverse that plan and send Wei water into the river?'

sentences.zh: 之錫從其言，並置衛河主簿，著為令。

translations.literal: Zhixi followed his words, and also established a Wei River chief clerk, setting it as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixi adopted the plan, appointed a chief clerk for the Wei River, and codified the practice.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，定運河修築工限：三年內衝決，參處修築官；

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, canal repair and construction time limits were fixed: within three years if breached by rush, the construction official was implicated;
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 the court set liability periods for canal works: breaches within three years implicated the building official;

sentences.zh: 過三年，參處防守官；

translations.literal: after three years, the defending official was implicated;
translations.idiomatic: after three years, the defending official;

sentences.zh: 不行防護，致有衝決，一併參處。

translations.literal: if protection was not carried out and a rush breach resulted, all were implicated together.
translations.idiomatic: if neglect of maintenance caused a breach, both were punished together.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，高郵大水，決運堤。

translations.literal: In the fourth year autumn, Gaoyou great flood, the transport dike burst.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year flooding at Gaoyou breached the canal dike.

sentences.zh: 五年，運河自儀徵至淮淤淺，知縣何崇倫募民夫濬之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the canal from Yizheng to the Huai was silted shallow; Magistrate He Chonglun recruited civilian laborers to dredge it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the canal from Yizheng to the Huai shoaled; Magistrate He Chonglun hired laborers to dredge it.

sentences.zh: 漕督林起龍言：「糧艘北行，處處阻閘阻淺，請飭河臣履勘安山、馬踏諸湖，暨各櫃閘子堤斗門堤岸，及東平、汶上諸泉，有無堵塞，務期濬泉清湖，以通運道。」

translations.literal: Grain Transport Director Lin Qilong said: 'Grain ships going north, everywhere blocked by locks and shallows—please order river officials to inspect on foot the lakes of Anshan, Mata, and others, together with each cabinet lock, child dike, sluice-gate dike and bank, and the springs of Dongping, Wenshang, and others, whether there is blockage or not; strive to dredge springs and clear lakes, to open the transport route.'
translations.idiomatic: Grain Transport Commissioner Lin Qilong urged: 'Northbound fleets meet locks and shallows at every turn. Order river officials to survey the Anshan and Mata lakes, every lock, auxiliary dike, and sluice, and the springs of Dongping and Wenshang for blockages, and dredge springs and lakes until the route is clear.'

sentences.zh: 六年，決江都露筋廟。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Jiangdu Lujin Temple section burst.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the dike failed at the Lujin Temple in Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 明年，塞之。

translations.literal: The next year, it was closed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year it was repaired.

sentences.zh: 十年，決高郵清水潭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Gaoyou Qingshui Pool section burst.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Qingshui Pool at Gaoyou breached.

sentences.zh: 明年，再決，十三年始塞。

translations.literal: The next year it burst again; only in the thirteenth year was it closed.
translations.idiomatic: It broke again the next year and was not sealed until the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 十四年，決江都邵伯鎮。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Jiangdu Shaobo town section burst.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the dike failed at Shaobo Town in Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏，久雨，漕堤崩潰，高郵清水潭、陸漫溝，江都大潭灣，共決三百餘丈。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year summer, long rain, the grain-transport dike collapsed; Gaoyou Qingshui Pool, Luman Ditch, Jiangdu Datang Bay—together more than three hundred zhang burst.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifteenth year prolonged rain collapsed the canal dike at Qingshui Pool and Luman Ditch in Gaoyou and Datang Bay in Jiangdu—over three hundred zhang in all.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以靳輔為河督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Jin Fu was made River Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Jin Fu was appointed Director-General of Rivers.

sentences.zh: 時東南水患益深，漕道益淺。

translations.literal: At the time southeastern water disasters grew deeper, and the grain route grew shallower.
translations.idiomatic: Flooding in the southeast worsened while the grain route shoaled further.

sentences.zh: 輔言：「河、運宜為一體。

translations.literal: Fu said: 'River and transport ought to be one body.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu argued: "River control and grain transport should be treated as one system.

sentences.zh: 運道之阻塞，率由河道之變遷。

translations.literal: Blockage of the transport route generally comes from changes in the river course.
translations.idiomatic: Canal blockages usually follow shifts in the river channel.

sentences.zh: 向來議治河者，多儘力於漕艘經行之地，其他決口，以為無關運道而緩視之，以致河道日壞，運道因之日梗。

translations.literal: Formerly those who discussed regulating the river mostly exerted strength on places grain ships passed; other breach points, thinking them unrelated to transport, they viewed lightly—so that the river course daily worsened and the transport route therefore daily clogged.
translations.idiomatic: Past river planners focused only where grain fleets sailed and neglected other breaches as irrelevant to transport; the main channel deteriorated and the canal followed.

sentences.zh: 是以原委相關之處，斷不容歧視也。

translations.literal: Therefore at places where origin and branch are related, divided regard absolutely cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Upstream and downstream must never be managed in isolation.

sentences.zh: 又運河自清口至清水潭，長約二百三十里，因黃內灌，河底淤高，居民日患沈溺，運艘每苦阻梗。

translations.literal: Again, the canal from Qingkou to Qingshui Pool, length about two hundred and thirty li—because the Yellow flowed inward, the river bottom silted high; residents daily suffered drowning, and transport ships constantly suffered obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: From Qingkou to Qingshui Pool, roughly two hundred thirty li, Yellow backflow had raised the bed: villagers faced flooding and grain ships constant delay.

sentences.zh: 請敕下各撫臣，將本年應運漕糧，務於明年三月內盡數過淮。

translations.literal: Please decree to each provincial governor that this year's grain due for transport must, by next year within the third month, all pass the Huai in full number.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the throne order every governor to move this year's tribute grain entirely across the Huai by the third month of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 俟糧艘過完，即封閉通濟閘壩，督集人夫，將運河大為挑濬，面寬十一丈，底寬三丈，深丈二尺，日役夫三萬四千七百有奇，三百日竣工。

translations.literal: When grain ships have all passed, immediately seal and close the Tongji lock dam, supervise gathering of laborers, and greatly dredge the canal—surface width eleven zhang, bottom width three zhang, depth one zhang two chi; daily laborers thirty-four thousand seven hundred odd, completion in three hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fleet has passed, close the Tongji dam, mobilize labor, and dredge the canal to eleven zhang wide at the surface, three at the bottom, and one zhang two chi deep, using over thirty-four thousand seven hundred laborers a day and finishing in three hundred days.

sentences.zh: 並堵塞清水潭、大潭灣決口六，及翟家壩至武家墩一帶決口，需帑九十八萬有奇。」

translations.literal: Together with closing six breach points at Qingshui Pool and Datang Bay, and the stretch of breaches from Zhaijiaba to Wujiadun, funds needed were nine hundred and eighty thousand odd.'
translations.idiomatic: Also close the six breaches at Qingshui Pool and Datang Bay and the breaches from Zhaijiaba to Wujiadun, at a cost of somewhat more than nine hundred eighty thousand taels."

sentences.zh: 又言：「向因河身淤墊，阻滯盤剝，艱苦萬端。

translations.literal: He also said: 'Formerly because the river body was silted and raised, obstruction and winching were delayed—hardships in ten thousand ways.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Previously, because the riverbed was silted up, obstruction, towing, and lightering caused every kind of hardship.

sentences.zh: 若清口一律浚深，則船可暢行，省費甚多。

translations.literal: If Qingkou were uniformly dredged deep, then ships could travel freely, saving much expense.
translations.idiomatic: Deepening Qingkou would let ships run freely and save large sums.

sentences.zh: 因令量輸所省之費，作治河之用，請俟運河浚深，船艘通行，凡過往貨物船，分別徵納剝淺銀數分，一年停止。」

translations.literal: Therefore he ordered measuring and delivering the saved expenses for river-regulation use, requesting that when the canal was dredged deep and ships could pass, all passing cargo boats should separately pay a few fen of shallow-lightening silver, stopping after one year.'
translations.idiomatic: I therefore ask that, once the canal has been dredged deep and boats can pass freely, passing cargo boats be charged a few fen of shallow-water levy according to type, using the saved expense for river works and stopping after one year."

sentences.zh: 均允行。

translations.literal: All were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 十七年，築江都漕堤，塞清水潭決口。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Jiangdu grain dike was built and the Qingshui Pool breach was closed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year workers built the Jiangdu canal dike and closed the Qingshui Pool breach.

sentences.zh: 清水潭逼近高郵湖，頻年潰決，隨築隨圮，決口寬至三百餘丈，大為漕艘患。

translations.literal: Qingshui Pool pressed close to Gaoyou Lake; year after year it burst and collapsed—as soon as built, so ruined—the breach width reaching more than three hundred zhang, a great affliction to grain ships.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshui Pool lay beside Gaoyou Lake and had breached repeatedly; repairs collapsed as fast as they rose, until the gap exceeded three hundred zhang and plagued grain fleets.

sentences.zh: 前年尚書冀如錫勘估工費五十七萬，夫柳仍派及民間，猶慮功不成。

translations.literal: The year before last Minister Ji Ruxi surveyed and estimated work costs at five hundred and seventy thousand; labor and willow materials were still assigned reaching to the populace, yet they still feared the work would not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Two years earlier Minister Ji Ruxi had estimated the repair at five hundred seventy thousand taels, with labor and fascines levied on the people, yet doubted it could succeed.

sentences.zh: 輔周視決口，就湖中離決口五六十丈為偃月形，抱兩端築之，成西堤一，長六百五丈，更挑繞西越河一，長八百四十丈，僅費帑九萬。

translations.literal: Fu circled the breach; in the lake fifty or sixty zhang from the breach he made a crescent shape, embracing both ends to build—forming one west dike, length six hundred and five zhang; further dredging a bypass west of the river, length eight hundred and forty zhang—spending only ninety thousand in treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu inspected the breach and, fifty or sixty zhang out in the lake, built a crescent embankment closing both ends—six hundred five zhang of west dike plus an eight-hundred-forty-zhang bypass to the west—for only ninety thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 至次年工竣。

translations.literal: By the next year the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The project finished the following year.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，名河曰永安，新河堤曰永安堤。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it, naming the river Yong'an and the new river dike the Yong'an Dike.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the work and named the channel Yong'an ('Ever Peace') and its dike the Yong'an Embankment.

sentences.zh: 是歲挑山、清、高、寶、江五州縣運河，塞決口三十二。

translations.literal: That year the canal was dredged in the five prefectures and counties of Shan, Qing, Gao, Bao, and Jiang, and thirty-two breach points were closed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the canal was dredged across five counties—Shanyang, Qingjiangpu, Gaoyou, Baoying, and Jiangdu—and thirty-two breaches were sealed.

sentences.zh: 輔又請按里設兵，分駐運堤，自清口至邵伯鎮南，每兵管兩岸各九十丈，責以栽柳蓄草，密種菱荷蒲葦，為永遠護岸之策。

translations.literal: Fu also requested setting soldiers by li, stationed separately on the transport dike from Qingkou to south of Shaobo Town—each soldier overseeing ninety zhang on each of both banks, charged to plant willows and store grass, densely planting water chestnut, lotus, cattail, and reed, as a policy for forever protecting the banks.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to post troops along the dike from Qingkou to south of Shaobo, each man responsible for ninety zhang on both banks, planting willows, grass, lotus, and reeds as a permanent revetment.

sentences.zh: 又言：「運河既議挑深，若不束淮入河濟運，仍容黃流內灌，不久復淤。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The canal having been discussed for deep dredging—if the Huai is not bound to enter the river to aid transport, and the Yellow current is still allowed inward flow, before long it will silt again.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Once the canal is to be dredged deep, if the Huai is not bound into the river to support transport and Yellow River flow is still allowed to back in, it will silt up again before long.

sentences.zh: 請於高堰堤工單薄處，幫修坦坡，為久遠衛堤計。」

translations.literal: Please at weak places in the Gaoyan dike works add repair with gentle slopes, as a long-term plan to guard the dike.'
translations.idiomatic: Please buttress the thin sections of the Gaoyan dike works with gentle slopes, as a long-term plan to protect the dike."

sentences.zh: 均如所議行。

translations.literal: All were carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 十八年，決山陽戚家橋，隨塞。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the Shanyang Qijia Bridge section burst and was soon closed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the dike failed at Qijia Bridge in Shanyang and was repaired at once.

sentences.zh: 明初江南各漕，自瓜、儀至清江浦，由天妃閘入黃。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming, the various Jiangnan grain routes from Guazhou and Yizheng to Qingjiangpu entered the Yellow through the Tianfei lock.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Ming, Jiangnan grain from Guazhou and Yizheng to Qingjiangpu entered the Yellow River at the Tianfei Lock.

sentences.zh: 後黃水內灌，潘季馴始移運口於新莊閘，納清避黃，仍以天妃名。

translations.literal: Later Yellow water flowed inward; Pan Jixun first moved the transport mouth to the Xinzhuang lock, admitting clear and avoiding Yellow, still using the Tianfei name.
translations.idiomatic: When Yellow water backed in, Pan Jixun moved the transport entrance to Xinzhuang Lock to draw clear water and avoid the Yellow, while keeping the Tianfei name.

sentences.zh: 然口距黃、淮交會處僅二百丈，黃仍內灌，運河墊高，年年挑濬無已。

translations.literal: Yet the mouth was only two hundred zhang from where the Yellow and Huai met; the Yellow still flowed inward, the canal bed was raised by silt, and year after year dredging had no end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the mouth lay only two hundred zhang from the Yellow–Huai confluence; Yellow water still backed in, raising the canal bed and forcing endless annual dredging.

sentences.zh: 兼以黃、淮會合，瀠洄激蕩，重運出口，危險殊甚。

translations.literal: Moreover, where the Yellow and Huai joined, swirling eddies surged and churned—the heavy-laden transport exit was exceptionally perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Where the two rivers met, swirling currents made the outlet for northbound grain fleets especially dangerous.

sentences.zh: 至是，輔議移南運口於爛泥淺之上，自新莊閘西南挑河一，至太平壩，又自文華寺永濟河頭起挑河一，南經七里閘，轉而西南，亦接太平壩，俱遠爛泥淺。

translations.literal: At this point Fu proposed moving the southern transport mouth above Lanni Shoal—from Xinzhuang lock southwest dredging one channel to Taiping Dam; again from Wenhua Temple at the head of the Yongji River dredging one channel, south passing Qili lock, turning southwest, also joining Taiping Dam—all far from Lanni Shoal.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu then proposed shifting the southern entrance above Lanni Shoal: one cut southwest from Xinzhuang to Taiping Dam, another from Wenhua Temple on the Yongji River south through Qili Lock and southwest to the same dam—both routes bypassing Lanni Shoal.

sentences.zh: 引河內兩渠並行，互為月河，以舒急溜，而爛泥淺一河，分十之二佐運，仍挾十之八射黃，黃不內灌，並難抵運口。

translations.literal: Within the diversion river two channels ran parallel, each a moon-river to the other, to ease the swift current; while the Lanni Shoal channel divided two-tenths to aid transport and still carried eight-tenths to shoot at the Yellow—the Yellow did not flow inward, and also could hardly reach the transport mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Two parallel channels served as mutual bypasses to ease the current; two-tenths of Lanni Shoal's flow fed transport while eight-tenths was aimed at the Yellow, keeping Yellow water out and away from the transport mouth.

sentences.zh: 由是重運過淮，揚帆直上，如履坦途。

translations.literal: Hence heavy transport crossing the Huai raised sails and went straight up, as if treading a level road.
translations.idiomatic: Northbound grain fleets could then cross the Huai under sail as on open water.

sentences.zh: 是歲開滾水壩於江都鰍魚骨，創建宿遷、桃源、清河、安東減壩六。

translations.literal: That year overflow dams were opened at Jiangdu Qiuyu Bone; six relief dams were newly created at Suqian, Taoyuan, Qinghe, and Andong.
translations.idiomatic: That year an overflow dam was opened at Qiuyu Bone in Jiangdu and six relief dams were built at Suqian, Taoyuan, Qinghe, and Andong.

sentences.zh: 十九年，創建鳳陽廠減壩一，碭山毛城鋪、大谷山，宿遷攔馬河、歸仁堤，邳州東岸馬家集減壩十一。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, one relief dam was newly created at Fengyang Works; at Dangshan Maochengpu and Dagu Mountain; at Suqian Lanma River and Guiren Dike; and eleven relief dams at Majiaji on the east bank of Pizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year one relief dam was built at Fengyang Works, works were done at Maochengpu and Dagu Mountain in Dangshan, at Lanma River and Guiren Dike in Suqian, and eleven relief dams on the east bank of Pizhou at Majiaji.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，糧艘抵宿遷，由董口北達。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, grain ships reaching Suqian went north through Dongkou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi, grain fleets reaching Suqian continued north through Dongkou.

sentences.zh: 後董口淤塞，遂取道駱馬湖。

translations.literal: Later Dongkou silted and blocked, and therefore they took the route through Luoma Lake.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongkou silted up, they routed through Luoma Lake.

sentences.zh: 湖淺水面闊，纖纜無所施，舟泥濘不得前，挑掘舁送，宿邑騷然。

translations.literal: The lake was shallow and the water surface wide—tow ropes had nowhere to apply; boats mired in mud could not advance; digging and carrying them forward—the Su county region was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The lake was shallow and broad: towlines could not grip, boats stuck in mud, and digging and hauling them through threw Suqian into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 輔因創開皁河四十里，上接泇河，下達黃河，漕運便之。

translations.literal: Fu therefore newly opened the Zao River forty li, upstream connecting to the Si River, downstream reaching the Yellow River—grain transport was made convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu therefore cut the forty-li Zao River, linking the Si River above to the Yellow below, and eased grain transport.

sentences.zh: 是歲霪兩，淮、黃並漲，決興化漕堤，水入高郵治，壞泗州城郭，特築滾壩於高郵南八里，及寶應之子嬰溝。

translations.literal: That year incessant rain, the Huai and Yellow both rose, the Xinghua grain dike burst, water entered Gaoyou seat, Sizhou walls and suburbs were ruined; overflow dams were specially built eight li south of Gaoyou and at Ziying Ditch in Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains that year raised both the Huai and Yellow, breached the Xinghua canal dike, flooded Gaoyou, and damaged Sizhou; overflow dams were built eight li south of Gaoyou and at Ziying Ditch in Baoying.

sentences.zh: 二十年七月，黃水大漲，皁河淤淀，不能通舟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, Yellow water greatly rose; the Zao River silted and settled, and could not pass boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twentieth year a Yellow flood silted the Zao River and blocked navigation.

sentences.zh: 眾議欲仍由駱馬湖，輔力持不可，親督挑掘丈餘，黃落清出，仍刷成河。

translations.literal: The multitude discussed wishing again to go by Luoma Lake; Fu strongly held it could not be done, personally supervised dredging of more than one zhang—the Yellow fell and clear emerged, and again it was scoured into a river.
translations.idiomatic: Many urged returning to Luoma Lake, but Jin Fu refused, personally supervised dredging more than one zhang deep until the Yellow dropped and clear water restored the channel.

sentences.zh: 隨閉皁河口攔黃壩，於迤東龍岡岔路口至張家莊挑新河三千餘丈，使出皁河，石磡之清水盡由新河行，至張家莊入黃河，是為張庄運口。

translations.literal: Then the Zao River mouth Yellow-blocking dam was closed; from Longgang fork eastward to Zhang Family Village a new river of more than three thousand zhang was dredged, causing exit from the Zao River—the clear water of Shikan all went by the new river, entering the Yellow River at Zhang Family Village—this was the Zhangzhuang transport mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He then closed the Yellow-blocking dam at the Zao mouth and cut a new channel of over three thousand zhang from Longgang east to Zhang Family Village so clear water from Shikan reached the Yellow at Zhangzhuang—the Zhangzhuang transport entrance.

sentences.zh: 是歲增築高郵南北滾水壩八，對壩均開越河，以防舟行之險，凡舊堤險處，皆更以石。

translations.literal: That year eight overflow dams north and south of Gaoyou were added and built; opposite each dam a bypass river was opened, to guard against the peril of boat travel; wherever old dikes were dangerous, all were replaced with stone.
translations.idiomatic: Eight overflow dams were added north and south of Gaoyou, each with a bypass channel to ease navigation, and hazardous stretches of the old dike were faced in stone.

sentences.zh: 二十二年九月，黃河由龍岡漫入，新河又淤。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year, the Yellow River overflowed in from Longgang; the new river silted again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year Yellow water poured in at Longgang and the new channel silted again.

sentences.zh: 隨於石磡築攔黃壩，復設法疏導，旬餘，新河仍暢行。

translations.literal: Then at Shikan a Yellow-blocking dam was built; methods of dredging and guiding were again applied, and in ten-odd days the new river again ran freely.
translations.idiomatic: A Yellow-blocking dam was built at Shikan and dredging resumed; within ten days the new channel was open again.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上南巡閱河，至清口，以運口水緊，令添建石閘於清河運口。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the emperor on southern tour inspected the river, reaching Qingkou; because transport mouth water was tight, he ordered adding construction of a stone lock at the Qinghe transport mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the emperor toured the south, inspected the river at Qingkou, and ordered a stone lock added at the Qinghe transport mouth because the current ran too fast.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，輔以運道經黃河，風濤險惡，自駱馬湖鑿渠，歷宿遷、桃源至清河仲家莊出口，名曰中河。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because the transport route passed the Yellow River and wind and waves were perilous and fierce, Fu from Luoma Lake cut a channel, passing Suqian and Taoyuan to the outlet at Zhong Family Village in Qinghe—named the Middle Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Jin Fu, finding the route through the Yellow River too dangerous, cut a channel from Luoma Lake through Suqian and Taoyuan to Zhong Family Village in Qinghe—the Middle Canal.

sentences.zh: 糧船北上，出清口後，行黃河數里，即入中河，直達張庄運口，以避黃河百八十里之險。

translations.literal: Grain boats going north, after leaving Qingkou, traveled the Yellow River a few li, then entered the Middle Canal, reaching straight to the Zhangzhuang transport mouth, to avoid the hundred and eighty li of Yellow River peril.
translations.idiomatic: Northbound grain ships left Qingkou, sailed only a few li on the Yellow River, entered the Middle Canal, and reached Zhangzhuang—avoiding a hundred eighty li of Yellow River hazards.

sentences.zh: 議者多謂輔此功不在明陳瑄鑿清口下。

translations.literal: Many in discussion said Fu's achievement in this was not beneath Ming Chen Xuan's cutting of the lower Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Many held that this feat ranked with Chen Xuan's opening of the lower Qingkou under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 而按察使于成龍、漕督慕天顏先後劾輔開中河累民，上斥其阻撓。

translations.literal: Yet Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong and Grain Transport Director Mu Tianyan successively impeached Fu for opening the Middle Canal and burdening the people; the emperor rebuked them for obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong and Grain Transport Commissioner Mu Tianyan impeached Jin Fu for burdening the people; the emperor rebuked them for obstruction.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，復遣尚書張玉書、圖納，左都御史馬齊等往視，亦稱中河安流，舟楫甚便。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, again Ministers Zhang Yushu and Tuna, Left Censor-in-Chief Ma Qi, and others were sent to inspect; they also declared the Middle Canal flowed peacefully and boats were very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Ministers Zhang Yushu and Tuna and Censor-in-Chief Ma Qi inspected the works and reported that the Middle Canal ran smoothly and navigation was easy.

sentences.zh: 但逼近黃流，不便展寬，而里運河及駱馬湖之水俱入此河，窄恐難容，應於蕭家渡、楊家莊、新莊各建減壩，俾水大可宣洩；

translations.literal: But it pressed close to the Yellow current and was inconvenient to widen; moreover the li canal and Luoma Lake waters all entered this river—if narrow, they feared it could not contain them. Relief dams should be built at Xiaojiadu, Yang Family Village, and Xinzhuang, so when water was great it could be discharged;
translations.idiomatic: They noted that hugging the Yellow River left little room to widen the channel, while water from the local canal and Luoma Lake all fed into it and might overflow; relief dams should be built at Xiaojiadu, Yang Family Village, and Xinzhuang to discharge excess flow;

sentences.zh: 仲家閘口大直恐倒灌，應向東南斜挑以避黃流。

translations.literal: the Zhong Family lock mouth, being too straight, feared backflow; it should be dredged obliquely toward the southeast to avoid the Yellow current.
translations.idiomatic: and the straight Zhong Family lock mouth risked backflow, so the outlet should be cut obliquely southeast to avoid the Yellow current.

sentences.zh: 詔俟臨閱時定奪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered awaiting decision when the emperor inspected on site.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed that these matters would be decided when he inspected in person.

sentences.zh: 是歲大雨，中河決，淹清河民田數千頃。

translations.literal: That year there was heavy rain; the Middle Canal burst its banks and inundated several thousand qing of the common people's fields in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains that year breached the Middle Canal and flooded several thousand acres of farmland in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 明年春，上南巡，閱視河工，至宿遷支河口，謂諸臣曰：「河道關係漕運民生，地形水勢，隨時權變。

translations.literal: The next spring the emperor made a southern tour to inspect river works; reaching the branch-river mouth at Suqian, he told the ministers: "The river course bears on grain transport and the people's livelihood; terrain and water conditions must be adjusted as circumstances require.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, on his southern inspection of hydraulic works, the emperor reached the Suqian branch channel and told his ministers: "The waterway concerns both grain transport and the people's livelihood; the terrain and water conditions must be managed flexibly according to circumstance.

sentences.zh: 今觀此河狹隘，逼近黃岸，萬一黃堤潰決，失於防禦，中河、黃河將溷為一。

translations.literal: Now I see this river is narrow and cramped and presses close to the Yellow bank; if by chance the Yellow dike should burst and defense fail, the Middle Canal and the Yellow River will mingle into one.
translations.idiomatic: Now, looking at this channel, it is narrow and presses close against the Yellow River bank. If the Yellow River levee were ever breached and defenses failed, the Middle Canal and the Yellow River would merge into one.

sentences.zh: 此河開後，商民無不稱便，安識日後若何？」

translations.literal: After this river was opened, merchants and commoners all praised its convenience—who can know how it will be hereafter?"
translations.idiomatic: Since this channel was opened, merchants and commoners have all called it convenient, but who can know what will happen later?"

sentences.zh: 圖納、馬齊言：「臣等勘河時，正值大水，懼河隘不能容諸水，故議於迤北遙堤修減壩三，令由舊河形入海。」

translations.literal: Tuna and Ma Qi said: "When we surveyed the river we met great flood and feared the narrow channel could not hold all the waters; therefore we proposed building three relief dams on the distant dike to the north, letting [water] follow the old river form to the sea."
translations.idiomatic: Tuna and Ma Qi said: "When we surveyed the river, it happened to be in major flood. Fearing that the narrow channel could not contain all the water, we proposed building three relief dams on the northern distant embankment so the water would enter the sea along the old river form."

sentences.zh: 輔言：「臣意開此河，可束水入海，及濬畢觀之，漕艘亦可行。

translations.literal: Fu said: "My intent in opening this river was to channel water to the sea; when dredging was finished and we observed it, grain barges could also pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu said: "My intention in opening this channel was that it could bind the water and send it to the sea; after the dredging was finished, I saw that grain barges could also pass through it.

sentences.zh: 今若加增遙堤，以保固黃河堤岸，當可無慮。」

translations.literal: Now if the distant dike is further raised to secure the Yellow River banks, there should be no concern."
translations.idiomatic: If the distant embankment is now increased and strengthened to protect the Yellow River banks, there should be no cause for concern."

sentences.zh: 河督王新命言：「支河口止一鎮口閘，微山湖諸水甚大，遇淫潦不能支，必致潰決。

translations.literal: River Director Wang Xinming said: "The branch-river mouth has only the one Zhenkou lock; the waters of Weishan Lake and the rest are very great—meeting excessive floods it cannot bear them and will surely burst.
translations.idiomatic: River Superintendent Wang Xinming said: "At the branch-channel mouth there is only the Zhenkou sluice, while the waters of Weishan Lake are very large. In prolonged rains it cannot hold them and will certainly breach.

sentences.zh: 若於駱馬湖作減壩，令漲水入黃，再修築郯城禹王台，以御流入駱馬湖之水，令注沭河，則中河無慮。」

translations.literal: If relief dams are built at Luoma Lake to let swollen water enter the Yellow, and the Yuwang Terrace at Tancheng is rebuilt to block water flowing into Luoma Lake and direct it into the Shu River, then the Middle Canal need not be worried over."
translations.idiomatic: If relief dams are built at Luoma Lake to let floodwater enter the Yellow River, and Yuwang Terrace at Tancheng is rebuilt to block the waters flowing into Luoma Lake and make them enter the Shu River, then the Middle Canal will be safe."

sentences.zh: 上謂可仍開支河，其黃河運道，並存不廢。

translations.literal: The emperor said the branch river could still be kept open; the Yellow River transport route would both be retained and not abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that the branch channel should remain in service while the Yellow River shipping route was also preserved.

sentences.zh: 先是玉書等請閉攔馬河，事下總河，至是新命言：「攔馬河原以宣黃水異漲，似應仍留，水漲則開放，水平則閉，以免中河淤墊。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Yushu and others had requested closing the Lanma River; the matter was referred to the Grand Canal directorate; now Xinming said: "The Lanma River was originally to discharge abnormal swell of Yellow water—it seems it should still be kept: when water rises, open it; when level, close it—to avoid silting of the Middle Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Yushu and the others had asked to close the Lanma River. The matter was sent down to the river governor, and now Wang Xinming said: "The Lanma River was originally used to release exceptional rises of Yellow River water. It seems it should still be left in place: when the water rises, open it; when the water is level, close it, so that the Middle Canal is not silted up.

sentences.zh: 至駱馬湖三減壩，玉書等議留二座於堤內，減水入中河，又恐中河不能容，擬於迤東蕭家渡、楊家莊、新河口量建減壩宣洩。

translations.literal: As for the three relief dams at Luoma Lake, Yushu and others proposed leaving two inside the dike to reduce water into the Middle Canal, yet again feared the Middle Canal could not contain it, and planned to build relief dams at Xiaojiadu, Yang Family Village, and Xinhekou to the east for discharge.
translations.idiomatic: As for Luoma Lake's three relief dams, Zhang Yushu and the others proposed leaving two inside the levee to release water into the Middle Canal, but then feared that the Middle Canal could not contain it and planned to build additional relief dams eastward at Xiaojiadu, Yangjiazhuang, and Xinhekou to release it.

sentences.zh: 臣謂既以中河不能容，何必留此二壩之水減入中河，復從蕭家渡等處建壩，多此曲折？

translations.literal: I say: since it is already held that the Middle Canal cannot contain [the water], why leave water from these two dams to reduce into the Middle Canal, and again build dams at Xiaojiadu and elsewhere—so many twists and turns?
translations.idiomatic: In my view, if the Middle Canal cannot contain it, why leave the water from these two dams to be released into the Middle Canal and then build dams again at Xiaojiadu and the other places, adding this needless indirection?

sentences.zh: 不若將三壩俱留遙堤外，令由舊河形入海，於蕭家渡三處量留缺口二，酌水勢以宣塞之為愈。

translations.literal: Better to leave all three dams outside the distant dike, letting [water] follow the old river form to the sea; at the three Xiaojiadu places measure and leave two gaps, adjusting to the water force to discharge or block—that would be better.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to leave all three dams outside the distant embankment and let the water enter the sea along the old river form, while leaving two gaps at Xiaojiadu and the other places and opening or closing them according to the water's force.

sentences.zh: 郯城沭水口舊有禹王台，障遏水勢，會白馬河、沂河之水入駱馬湖，愈覺泛溢不可遏，應於台舊基迎水處堵塞斷流，令仍由故道入海。」

translations.literal: At the Shu River mouth in Tancheng there was formerly the Yuwang Terrace, checking water force and gathering the waters of the Baima and Yi rivers into Luoma Lake—the overflow felt ever harder to restrain; at the terrace's old base where water meets, the flow should be blocked and cut off, letting it still follow the old course to the sea."
translations.idiomatic: At the Shu River mouth in Tancheng there was formerly Yuwang Terrace, which blocked the water's force and caused the waters of the Baima and Yi rivers to enter Luoma Lake, making the flooding still more impossible to restrain. The water-facing side of the old terrace site should be closed off, cutting the flow and making the waters again enter the sea by their former course."

sentences.zh: 下扈從諸臣確議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the attending ministers for firm deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministers in his entourage to deliberate and settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 惟駱馬湖減壩用玉書等原議，餘如新命言。

translations.literal: Only the Luoma Lake relief dams followed Yushu and others' original proposal; the rest accorded with Xinming's views.
translations.idiomatic: They adopted Zhang Yushu's plan for the Luoma Lake relief dams but otherwise followed Wang Xinming's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，直隸運河決通州李家口等五口，天津耍兒渡等八口。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the Zhili Grand Canal burst at five places including Lijia Mouth in Tongzhou and at eight places including Shua'er Ferry in Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-two the Zhili canal broke in thirteen places, five near Tongzhou's Lijia Mouth and eight around Tianjin's Shua'er Ferry.

sentences.zh: 衛河微弱，惟恃漳為灌輸，由館陶分流濟運。

translations.literal: The Wei River was weak and relied only on the Zhang River for irrigation and transport, branching from Guantao to supplement the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: The feeble Wei River depended entirely on Zhang River water diverted at Guantao to feed the transport channel.

sentences.zh: 明隆、萬間，漳北徙入滏陽河，館陶之流遂絕。

translations.literal: Between the Longqing and Wanli reigns of Ming the Zhang shifted north into the Fuyang River, and Guantao's flow then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: During the late Ming the Zhang had shifted north into the Fuyang River, cutting off the Guantao diversion.

sentences.zh: 至是三十六年，忽分流，仍由館陶入衛濟運。

translations.literal: By the thirty-sixth year it suddenly branched again and still entered the Wei from Guantao to supplement transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-six the Zhang unexpectedly split anew and once more supplied the Wei and the canal through Guantao.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，廷議改高郵減壩及茆家園等六壩均為滾水壩，增加高堰石工五尺。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the court resolved to convert the Gaoyou relief dams and six dams including Maojiayuan into overflow dams, and to add five feet of stonework to the Gaoyan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the court replaced Gaoyou's relief dams and six others, including Maojiayuan, with rolling overflow dams and raised the Gaoyan stonework by five feet.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，上以清口日淤，恐誤糧艘，海道運津又極艱險，擬以沙船載糧，自江下海，至黃河入海之口，運入中河，則海運不遠。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, because Qingkou daily silted and he feared delaying grain fleets, and because the sea route to Tianjin was also extremely perilous, the emperor proposed using sand ships to carry grain from the Yangtze to sea, to the Yellow River's estuary, and then into the Middle Canal—so sea transport would not be far.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-nine, worried that silting at Qingkou would trap grain barges and that the coastal route to Tianjin was treacherous, the emperor proposed loading grain onto sand junks at the Yangtze, sailing to the Yellow estuary, and transshipping into the Middle Canal to shorten the sea leg.

sentences.zh: 下河督張鵬翮籌議。

translations.literal: The proposal was sent down to River Director Zhang Penghe to plan and discuss.
translations.idiomatic: He referred the scheme to Zhang Penghe, superintendent of rivers, for evaluation.

sentences.zh: 鵬翮言運河決口已塞，清水又已引出，糧船當可暢達。

translations.literal: Penghe said the canal breach mouths had already been sealed and clear water had again been drawn out; grain ships should pass freely.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Penghe reported that the breaches were closed, clear water had been restored, and the grain fleet could sail unimpeded.

sentences.zh: 若改載沙船，雇募水手，徒滋糜費。

translations.literal: If [grain] were shifted to sand ships and sailors hired, it would only increase wasteful expense.
translations.idiomatic: Switching to sand junks and hiring seamen, he argued, would merely waste money.

sentences.zh: 且由江入海，從黃河海口入中河，風濤不測，實屬難行。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the river to sea and from the Yellow River estuary into the Middle Canal, wind and waves are unpredictable—it is truly hard to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: The passage from the Yangtze through the open sea and the Yellow estuary into the Middle Canal, he added, was too exposed to storms to be practicable.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 初，河督于成龍以中河南逼黃河，難以築堤，乃自桃源盛家道口至清河，棄中河下段，改鑿六十里，名曰新中河。

translations.literal: Earlier, River Director Yu Chenglong, because the Middle Canal south pressed close to the Yellow River and dikes were hard to build, from Taoyuan's Shengjiadao mouth to Qinghe abandoned the lower section of the Middle Canal and cut a new channel of sixty li, named the New Middle Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong had earlier abandoned the lower Middle Canal where it hugged the Yellow River and, from Shengjiadao in Taoyuan to Qinghe, excavated a sixty-li bypass called the New Middle Canal.

sentences.zh: 至是，鵬翮見新中河淺狹，且盛家道口河頭灣曲，輓運不順，因於三義壩築攔河堤，截用舊中河上段、新中河下段合為一河，重加修濬，運道稱便。

translations.literal: By now Penghe saw that the New Middle Canal was shallow and narrow and that the river head at Shengjiadao mouth was winding so that hauling was not smooth; therefore at Sanyi Dam he built a blocking dike, joining the upper old Middle Canal and the lower New Middle Canal into one river, dredging it heavily again—the transport route was praised as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Penghe found the New Middle Canal too shallow and its head at Shengjiadao too tortuous for towing; he built a blocking embankment at Sanyi Dam, merged the upper old channel with the lower new cut, dredged the whole line, and restored an easy transport route.

sentences.zh: 四十年，以湖口清水已出，宜籌節宣之法，允鵬翮請，於張福口、裴家場二引河間，再開引河一，合力敵黃。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, because clear water had emerged at the lake mouth, methods of regulating discharge should be planned; Penghe's request was approved to open one more diversion river between the two diversion rivers at Zhangfukou and Peijia field, combining force to resist the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty, with clear water again issuing at the lake mouth, the court approved Zhang Penghe's plan to cut a third diversion between Zhangfukou and Peijiazhuang to bolster the fight against Yellow River backflow.

sentences.zh: 若黃漲在糧艘已過，堵攔黃壩，使不得倒灌；

translations.literal: If the Yellow rose after the grain fleets had passed, the Yellow-blocking dam should be sealed so it could not backflow;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow surged after the grain convoy had cleared, the blocking dam would be closed to prevent reverse flow;

sentences.zh: 漲在行船時，閉裴家場引河口，引清水入三汊河至文華寺濟運。

translations.literal: if the rise came while ships were under way, the Peijia field diversion mouth would be closed and clear water led through the San Cha River to Wenhua Temple to supplement transport.
translations.idiomatic: if the flood caught the fleet still moving, the Peijiazhuang intake would be shut and clear water routed through the San Cha River to Wenhua Temple to sustain shipping.

sentences.zh: 是歲建中河口南岸石閘。

translations.literal: That year a stone lock was built on the south bank of the Middle Canal mouth.
translations.idiomatic: That year they completed a masonry sluice on the south bank of the Middle Canal entrance.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，以仲庄徬清水出口，逼溜南趨，致礙運道，詔移中河運口於楊家莊，即大清水故道，由是漕鹽兩利。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, because Zhongzhuang adjoined the clear-water outlet and the current was forced south, impeding the transport route, an edict moved the Middle Canal transport mouth to Yang Family Village, on the old course of the great clear water—whereupon both grain transport and salt benefited.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-two, eddying at Zhongzhuang near the clear-water outlet was deflecting the current south and hindering traffic; the court relocated the Middle Canal shipping mouth to Yangjiazhuang on the former main clear-water channel, benefiting both grain and salt transport.

sentences.zh: 逾年，又命建直隸運河楊村減壩以分水勢。

translations.literal: The following year he again ordered a relief dam built at Yang Village on the Zhili Grand Canal to divide the water force.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he ordered a Yangcun spill dam on the Zhili canal to split flood pressure.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，上言高堰及運河減壩不開放，則危及堤堰，開泄又潦傷隴畝，宜於高堰三滾壩下挑河築堤，束水入高郵、邵伯諸湖，其減壩下亦挑河築堤，束水由串場溪注白駒、丁溪、草堰諸河入海。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year a memorial stated: if the Gaoyan and canal relief dams are not opened, the dikes are endangered; if opened and discharged, floods harm the fields—it is fitting below the three overflow dams of the Gaoyan to dredge a river and build dikes, channeling water into the lakes of Gaoyou and Shaobo; below the relief dams likewise dredge and build dikes, channeling water through Chuanchang Creek into the Baiju, Dingxi, and Caoyan rivers to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-four officials warned that keeping the Gaoyan and canal spillways closed endangered the levees, while opening them flooded farmland; they proposed channel works below the three Gaoyan overflow dams to send water into the Gaoyou and Shaobo lakes, and similar works below the relief dams to discharge through Chuanchang Creek into the Baiju, Dingxi, and Caoyan rivers to the sea.

sentences.zh: 令江、漕、河各督勘估，遣官督修。

translations.literal: The Jiangsu, grain-transport, and river superintendents were ordered each to survey and estimate, and officials were dispatched to supervise repairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangsu, grain-transport, and river governors were told to survey the works, estimate costs, and oversee construction.

sentences.zh: 自是淮、揚各郡悉免漫溢之患。

translations.literal: From then on all prefectures of Huai and Yang were entirely spared the calamity of inundation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Huai and Yang regions were largely freed from catastrophic flooding.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，鵬翮於中河橫堤建草壩二，鮑家營引河處建草壩一，相機啟閉，免中河淤墊。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year Penghe built two grass dams on the Middle Canal cross-dike and one grass dam at the Baojia Camp diversion, opening or closing them as conditions warranted to avoid silting of the Middle Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-five Zhang Penghe added two straw dams on the Middle Canal transverse levee and one at the Baojiaying diversion, operating them as needed to keep the canal from silting.

sentences.zh: 又以運河水漲，堤岸難容，於文華寺建石閘，閘下開引河，自楊家廟、單楊口迄白馬湖，長萬四千八百丈有奇，水漲開放入湖，水涸堵閉。

translations.literal: Also, because canal water rose and the banks could hardly contain it, at Wenhua Temple a stone lock was built; below the lock a diversion river was opened from Yang Family Temple and Danyang mouth to Baima Lake, more than fourteen thousand eight hundred zhang in length—when water rose it was opened into the lake, when water fell it was blocked closed.
translations.idiomatic: When rising canal levels threatened the banks, he built a stone sluice at Wenhua Temple with a fourteen-thousand-eight-hundred-zhang bypass to Baima Lake through Yangjiamiao and Danyangkou, opened in flood and sealed in drought.

sentences.zh: 是年，濟寧道張伯行請引漳自成安柏寺營通漳之新河，接館陶之沙河，古所謂馬頰河者，疏其淤塞，使暢流入衛。

translations.literal: That year Jining Circuit Intendant Zhang Boxing requested drawing the Zhang River from Bosi Camp in Cheng'an along the new river connecting to the Zhang, joining the Sha River at Guantao—the river anciently called the Majia—dredging its silt so it would flow freely into the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Boxing, intendant of the Jining circuit, petitioned to divert the Zhang from Cheng'an through the Tongzhang New River into the Sha River at Guantao along the ancient Majia channel, clearing obstructions so it could feed the Wei.

sentences.zh: 議未及行。

translations.literal: The proposal was discussed but not yet carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was debated but not implemented.

sentences.zh: 越二年，全漳入館陶，漳、衛合而勢悍急，恩、德當沖受害，乃於德州哨馬營、恩縣四女寺建壩，開支河以殺其勢。

translations.literal: Two years later the entire Zhang entered Guantao; the Zhang and Wei merged and their force was fierce and swift; Enzhou and Dezhou bore the brunt and suffered harm; dams were then built at Shaomaying in Dezhou and Sinv Temple in En County, and branch rivers opened to reduce the force.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on the full Zhang flow returned to Guantao, combining with the Wei in a violent torrent that battered En and De; spill dams at Dezhou's Shaomaying and En County's Sinv Temple and branch channels were built to tame it.

sentences.zh: 六十年，東撫李樹德請開彭口新河。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year Shandong Governor Li Shude requested opening the Pengkou New River.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixty Shandong governor Li Shude petitioned to open the Pengkou New River.

sentences.zh: 先是濟寧道某言，彭口一帶有昭陽、微山、西湖，噴沙積於三洞橋內，屢開屢塞，阻滯糧艘，應挑新河、避噴沙，以疏運道。

translations.literal: Earlier an official of the Jining circuit had said that around Pengkou, where Zhaoyang, Weishan, and West lakes lie, gushing sand accumulated inside Sandong Bridge—repeatedly opened and repeatedly blocked, obstructing grain fleets; a new river should be dredged to avoid the gushing sand and clear the transport route.
translations.idiomatic: A Jining official had earlier reported that sand spitting from Zhaoyang, Weishan, and West lakes kept choking the channel inside Sandong Bridge despite repeated dredging, blocking grain traffic; a new cut was needed to bypass the sand fan.

sentences.zh: 至是，樹德以為言。

translations.literal: By now Shude submitted the same proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shude now renewed that petition.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「山東運河，自西湖之水流入。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Shandong Grand Canal receives the inflow from West Lake.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Shandong canal is supplied by water flowing in from West Lake.

sentences.zh: 前此百姓以為宜開即開，以為宜閉亦閉。

translations.literal: Before this, whenever the common people thought opening fit, it was opened; whenever they thought closing fit, it was closed.
translations.idiomatic: Locals had long opened or closed channels as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 開者何意？

translations.literal: What was the intent in opening?
translations.idiomatic: What did they hope to gain by opening it?

sentences.zh: 堵者何意？

translations.literal: What was the intent in blocking?
translations.idiomatic: And what did they hope to gain by blocking it?

sentences.zh: 務悉其故，方可定其開否。

translations.literal: The reasons must be fully understood—only then can it be decided whether to open or not.
translations.idiomatic: Only when their reasons are fully understood can it be decided whether to open the river.

sentences.zh: 不然，虛耗矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the effort is wasted in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the funds will simply be wasted."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「山東運河，全賴湖、泉濟運。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Shandong Grand Canal wholly relies on lakes and springs to supplement transport.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The Shandong canal relies entirely on lakes and springs to support transport.

sentences.zh: 今多開稻田，截上流以資灌溉，湖水自然無所蓄瀦，安能濟運？

translations.literal: Now many paddy fields are opened and upper streams are intercepted for irrigation—naturally lake water has nowhere to store and pond; how can it supplement transport?
translations.idiomatic: Now many rice fields have been opened, and upstream water is intercepted for irrigation, so the lake water naturally has nowhere to be stored. How can it support transport?

sentences.zh: 往年東民欲開新河，朕恐下流泛濫，禁而弗許。

translations.literal: In prior years the eastern people wished to open a new river; I feared flooding of the lower reach and forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: In past years the people of the east wanted to open a new channel, but I feared flooding downstream and forbade it.

sentences.zh: 今又請開新河。

translations.literal: Now they again request opening a new river.
translations.idiomatic: Now they again ask to open a new channel.

sentences.zh: 此地一面為微山湖，一面為嶧縣諸山，更從何處開鑿耶？

translations.literal: This place has Weishan Lake on one side and the mountains of Yixian on the other—from where else could excavation proceed?
translations.idiomatic: With Weishan Lake on one side of this place and the hills of Yixian on the other, where else could they dig?

sentences.zh: 張鵬翮到東，將此旨詳諭巡撫，申飭地方，相度泉源，蓄積湖水，俾漕運無誤，自易易耳。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Penghe reaches the east, let this edict be explained in detail to the governor; instruct the locality, survey spring sources, and store lake water so that grain transport is not in error—that is easy indeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Penghe reaches Shandong, he should explain this decree fully to the governor, admonish the local officials, survey the springs, and store up lake water so that grain transport is not delayed. That is easily done."

translations.literal: Thus ended the imperial address.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ended the imperial address.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，河督齊蘇勒偕漕督張大有言：「山東蓄水濟運，有南旺、馬踏、蜀山、安山、馬場、昭陽、獨山、微山、郗山等湖，水漲則引河水入湖，涸則引湖水入槽，隨時收蓄，接應運河，古人名曰『水櫃』。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, River Superintendent Qi Sule together with Grain Transport Director Zhang Dayou said: "To store water in Shandong and supplement transport there are the lakes Nanwang, Mata, Shushan, Anshan, Machang, Zhaoyang, Dushan, Weishan, Xishan, and others—when water rises, river water is led into the lakes; when dry, lake water is led into the channel; storing and releasing according to the season, they meet the Grand Canal—the ancients called them 'water cabinets.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 Qi Sule and Zhang Dayou described Shandong's chain of storage lakes—from Nanwang, Mata, and Shushan to Weishan and beyond—as ancient "water cabinets" that filled from the river in flood and fed the canal in drought.

sentences.zh: 歷年既久，昭陽、安山、南旺多為居民占種私墾。

translations.literal: Over many years Zhaoyang, Anshan, and Nanwang have largely been occupied and privately reclaimed by residents.
translations.idiomatic: Decades of encroachment had turned much of Zhaoyang, Anshan, and Nanwang into private farmland.

sentences.zh: 現除已成田不追外，餘俟水落丈量，樹立封界，永禁侵佔，設法收蓄。

translations.literal: What has already become fields will not be reclaimed; the rest, when water falls, will be measured, boundary markers erected, encroachment forever forbidden, and methods devised for storage.
translations.idiomatic: They would not dispossess established fields but would survey the remaining lakebed after drawdown, mark boundaries, forbid further encroachment, and restore storage capacity.

sentences.zh: 至馬踏、蜀山、馬場、南陽諸湖，原有斗門閘座，加以土壩，可收蓄深廣，備來年濟運之資。

translations.literal: As for the lakes Mata, Shushan, Machang, and Nanyang, which originally had sluice towers and could receive earthen dams, they can be stored deep and wide as resources for next year's transport.
translations.idiomatic: Mata, Shushan, Machang, and Nanyang still had sluice towers and could be deepened behind earthen dams to stock water for the coming transport season.

sentences.zh: 惟獨山一湖，濱臨運河，一線小堰，且多缺口。

translations.literal: Only Dushan Lake, bordering the Grand Canal with a single narrow levee and many gaps, [is problematic].
translations.idiomatic: Dushan Lake alone, pressed against the canal by a thin, broken embankment, needed special attention.

sentences.zh: 相度水勢，河水盛漲，聽其灌入湖中；

translations.literal: Surveying the water force, when river water greatly rises, let it be allowed to pour into the lake;
translations.idiomatic: When the river ran high, they would let it fill Dushan;

sentences.zh: 湖、河平，即築堰堵截；

translations.literal: when lake and river are level, immediately build the levee and block;
translations.idiomatic: when levels equalized, they would seal the embankment;

sentences.zh: 河水稍落，不使湖水走泄涓滴。

translations.literal: when the river falls slightly, not a drop of lake water is to be allowed to escape.
translations.idiomatic: and as the river fell they would hold every drop in the lake.

sentences.zh: 或遇運河淺塞，則引湖水下注，庶幾接濟便捷。

translations.literal: If the Grand Canal is shallow or blocked, then lake water is led down to supplement—thus connection and aid are convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Stored water could then be released whenever the canal ran shallow.

sentences.zh: 至諸湖閘座，仍照舊例，灌塘積水，啟閉以時，則湖水深廣，運道疏通矣。」

translations.literal: As for sluices on the various lakes, still follow the old practice of filling ponds and opening and closing on schedule—then lake water will be deep and broad and the transport route cleared."
translations.idiomatic: Maintaining the traditional sluice regimen, they argued, would keep the lakes full and the transport channel open."

sentences.zh: 下所司議行。

translations.literal: The proposal was sent down to the relevant offices for discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred the plan to the appropriate agencies for action.

sentences.zh: 二年，齊蘇勒以駱馬湖東岸低洼易泄，舊壩不足抵禦，於湖東陸塘河通寧橋西高地築攔河滾壩，再築攔水堤六百丈，口門寬三十丈，以便宣洩。

translations.literal: In the second year Qi Sule, because the east bank of Luoma Lake was low-lying and easy to leak and the old dams were insufficient to resist, at Lutang River east of the lake built a blocking overflow dam west of Tongning Bridge on the high ground, and again built a water-blocking dike six hundred zhang long with a mouth thirty zhang wide for discharge.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 Qi Sule reinforced Luoma Lake's low eastern shore with a rolling dam west of Tongning Bridge on the Lutang River and a six-hundred-zhang spill embankment with a thirty-zhang outlet.

sentences.zh: 又幫築運河西岸地洞口堤身五百十丈，高、寶、江東西岸堤工五千二十四丈，寶應西堤七里閘迤南至柳園頭埽工五百七十丈。

translations.literal: He also assisted in building five hundred ten zhang of dike body at the cave mouth on the west bank of the canal, and five thousand twenty-four zhang of dike works on the east and west banks of Gaoyou and Baoying, and five hundred seventy zhang of revetment from Qili Lock south of Baoying's west dike to Liuyuantou.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped repair five hundred ten zhang of west-bank works at the canal intake, more than five thousand zhang of levees around Gaoyou and Baoying, and five hundred seventy zhang of revetment south from Qili Lock to Liuyuantou.

sentences.zh: 四年，齊蘇勒改種家渡南之舊彭口於十字河，而彭口沙壅積如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Qi Sule moved the old Pengkou south of Zhongjiadu to the Cross River, yet sand still accumulated and blocked Pengkou as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Qi Sule relocated the old Pengkou below Zhongjiadu to the Cross River, but sand continued to choke the mouth as before.

sentences.zh: 先是侍郎蔣陳錫疏陳漕運事宜，上命內閣學士何國宗等勘視豫東運道，至是覆稱：「山東運河必賴湖水接濟，請將安山湖開濬築堤；

translations.literal: Earlier Vice Minister Jiang Chenxi had memorialized on grain transport affairs; the emperor ordered Academician He Guozong and others to inspect the transport route east of Henan; now their report said: "The Shandong Grand Canal must rely on lake water for supplementation; Anshan Lake should be dredged and diked;
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Chenxi's memorial on transport and He Guozong's inspection of the Henan-Shandong canal, the reviewers reported: "The Shandong canal must rely on lake water for support. We ask that Anshan Lake be dredged and embanked;

sentences.zh: 南旺、馬踏諸堤及關家壩俱加高培厚，建石閘以時啟閉；

translations.literal: the dikes of Nanwang, Mata, and the rest and Guanjia Dam should all be raised and thickened, and stone locks built to open and close on schedule;
translations.idiomatic: the Nanwang and Mata levees and Guanjia Dam should all be heightened and thickened, and stone sluices should be built to open and close at the proper times;

sentences.zh: 其分水口兩岸沙山下，各築束水壩一；

translations.literal: below each division mouth on both banks under the sand hills, one water-channeling dam should be built;
translations.idiomatic: below the sandy hills on both banks of each water-dividing mouth, one training dam should be built;

sentences.zh: 汶水南戴村壩應加修築；

translations.literal: the Dai Village Dam on the south Wen River should be repaired;
translations.idiomatic: the Dai Village Dam on the southern Wen should be strengthened;

sentences.zh: 建坎河石壩於汶水北；

translations.literal: a stone overflow dam should be built on the north Wen at Kan River;
translations.idiomatic: a stone dam should be built at Kan River on the northern Wen;

sentences.zh: 恩縣四女寺應建挑壩一；

translations.literal: at Sinv Temple in En County one training dam should be built;
translations.idiomatic: one training dam should be built at Sinv Temple in En County;

sentences.zh: 專平運河西岸修復進水關二，東岸建滾壩一；

translations.literal: on the west bank of the canal exclusively, two intake locks should be restored; on the east bank one overflow dam should be built;
translations.idiomatic: two intake locks should be restored on the west bank of the Zhuanping canal, and one overflow dam should be built on the east bank;

sentences.zh: 濮州沙河會趙王河處，舊有土壩引河，應修築開濬，其河西州縣，聽民開通水道，匯入沙河，於運道民生，均有裨益；

translations.literal: at the confluence of the Sha and Zhao Wang rivers in Puzhou, where there was formerly an earthen dam diversion, it should be repaired and dredged; west of the river the prefectures and counties may open waterways for the people to join the Sha River—benefiting both transport and livelihood;
translations.idiomatic: where the Sha River meets the Zhao Wang River in Puzhou, the old earthen dam and diversion channel should be repaired and dredged, and the prefectures and counties west of the river should be allowed to open water channels feeding into the Sha River, benefiting both the transport route and the people's livelihood;

sentences.zh: 武城及恩縣北岸，各挑引河一。

translations.literal: on the north banks of Wucheng and En County, one diversion river each should be dredged.
translations.idiomatic: one diversion channel should be dug on each of the north banks of Wucheng and En County.

sentences.zh: 河南運河自北泉而下，歷仁、義、禮、智、信五閘，遏水旁註，愚民不無截流盜水之弊。

translations.literal: The Henan Grand Canal from Beiquan downward passes through the five locks Ren, Yi, Li, Zhi, and Xin, which hold back water for lateral discharge—among the foolish people there is no lack of the abuse of intercepting flow and stealing water.
translations.idiomatic: Below Beiquan, the Henan canal passes through the five locks named Ren, Yi, Li, Zhi, and Xin; by checking water and diverting it sideways, they give ignorant people opportunities to cut off the flow and steal water.

sentences.zh: 請拆去五閘，於泉池南口建石堰一，開口門三，分為三渠，築小堤使無旁泄；

translations.literal: It is requested to remove the five locks and build one stone weir at the south mouth of the spring pool with three openings, divided into three channels, small dikes built so there is no lateral leakage;
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the five locks be removed, that one stone weir be built at the southern mouth of the spring pool, with three gates opened into three channels, and that small levees be built so there is no side leakage;

sentences.zh: 東西各開一渠，渠各建五閘，分溉民田。

translations.literal: east and west each open one channel; each channel builds five locks to irrigate the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: one channel should be opened on each of the east and west sides, with five sluices in each channel, to divide irrigation for the people's fields.

sentences.zh: 小丹河自清化鎮下應開濬築小堤，河東一里開水塘一，石閘三，分為三渠，以小丹河為官渠，東西各一為民渠。

translations.literal: The Xiaodan River below Qinghua Town should be dredged and small dikes built; east of the river one pond every li, three stone locks, divided into three channels—with the Xiaodan as the official channel and one each east and west for the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaodan River below Qinghua town should be dredged and given small levees; one pond and three stone sluices should be opened one li east of the river and divided into three channels, with the Xiaodan River as the official channel and one channel each to east and west as people's channels.

sentences.zh: 其洹河石壩皆已湮廢，宜增修為挑壩。

translations.literal: The stone dams on the Huan River have all been buried and ruined; they should be increased and repaired as training dams.
translations.idiomatic: The stone dams on the Huan River have all become silted and ruined and should be enlarged and repaired as training dams.

sentences.zh: 諸泉源應各開深廣，入衛濟運。」

translations.literal: Each spring source should be opened deep and broad to enter the Wei and supplement transport."
translations.idiomatic: All the spring heads should be opened deeper and wider so they enter the Wei and support transport."

sentences.zh: 下所司議行。

translations.literal: The report was sent down to the relevant offices for discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The court again ordered the responsible agencies to act on the report.

sentences.zh: 五年，東撫塞楞額以柳長河日見淤淺，雖一帶相連，而中有金錢嶺分隔，特開引河二，一從嶺北注安山入湖，一從嶺南出閘口濟運。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Shandong Governor Saileng'e, because the Willow Long River daily grew shallower—though one continuous strip, the Jinqian Ridge divided it—specially opened two diversion rivers: one from north of the ridge pouring into Anshan and the lake, one from south of the ridge exiting the lock mouth to supplement transport.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Governor Saileng'e, finding the Willow Long River silting despite its continuity, cut two diversions around Jinqian Ridge—one north into Anshan Lake, one south through the lock to feed the canal.

sentences.zh: 八年，河督嵇曾筠言：「宿遷駱馬湖舊有十字河口門，引湖濟運，兼以刷黃。

translations.literal: In the eighth year River Superintendent Ji Zengjun said: "At Suqian on Luoma Lake there was formerly the Cross River mouth, drawing lake water to supplement transport and also to scour the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight River Superintendent Ji Zengjun said: "Suqian's Luoma Lake formerly had the Cross River mouth, which drew lake water to support transport and also scoured the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 嗣湖水微弱，恐黃倒灌，堵閉河口，又於西寧橋迤西建攔湖壩，因是湖水不通，專資黃濟運，致中河之水挾沙淤墊。

translations.literal: Subsequently, when lake water grew weak and they feared Yellow backflow, the river mouth was blocked; west of Xining Bridge a lake-blocking dam was built—thus lake water did not communicate and they relied solely on the Yellow to supplement transport, causing Middle Canal water to carry sand and silt.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the lake water weakened, people feared Yellow River backflow, closed the river mouth, and also built a lake-blocking dam west of Xining Bridge. Because of this, lake water no longer passed through, transport relied solely on the Yellow River, and the Middle Canal's water carried sand and silted up.

sentences.zh: 今秋山水暴漲，去路遏塞，漫溢橫出。

translations.literal: This autumn mountain floods swelled violently; the outlet was blocked and water overflowed horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: This autumn mountain floods rose violently, their route was blocked, and they spilled out crosswise.

sentences.zh: 請復十字河舊口門，俾湖水入中河，刷深運道，攔湖壩酌量開寬，俾上游之水，由六塘河入海。」

translations.literal: It is requested to restore the old Cross River mouth so lake water enters the Middle Canal and scours the transport route deep; the lake-blocking dam should be suitably widened so upstream water goes out through the Liutang River to the sea."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the old Cross River mouth be restored so lake water can enter the Middle Canal and scour the transport route deeper, and that the lake-blocking dam be widened as appropriate so upstream water enters the sea by the Liutang River."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 是年始設黃、運兩岸守堤堡夫，二里一堡，堡設夫二，住堤巡守，遠近互為聲援。

translations.literal: That year they first established dike-guard posts on both banks of the Yellow and transport rivers—one post every two li, each post with two laborers dwelling on the dike to patrol, mutual support near and far.
translations.idiomatic: That year also saw the first patrol posts every two li along the Yellow and canal banks, each manned by two guards who could call on neighbors for help.

sentences.zh: 九年，兼總河田文鏡言：「汶南流濟運，向有玲瓏及亂石、滾水三壩。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Combined River Director Tian Wenjing said: "The Wen flowing south supplements transport; formerly there were the Linglong and Luanshi overflow dams and the rolling-water dam.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine, Tian Wenjing, concurrently director-general of rivers, said: "The southern-flowing Wen supports transport and formerly had the three dams of Linglong, Luanshi, and Gunshui.

sentences.zh: 伏秋盛漲，水由滾壩入鹽河，沙由玲瓏、亂石洞隙隨水滾瀉。

translations.literal: In the height of summer flood the water entered the Salt River through the rolling dam, and sand rolled out through the crevices of Linglong and Luanshi.
translations.idiomatic: During the great summer and autumn rises, water entered the Salt River through the rolling dam, while sand rolled out with the water through the gaps at Linglong and Luanshi.

sentences.zh: 自何國宗於三壩內增建石壩，涓滴不通，既無尾閭泄水，又無罅隙通淤，致汶挾沙入運，淤積日高。

translations.literal: Since He Guozong built stone dams inside the three dams so that not a drop passed, there was neither tail outlet to discharge water nor crevice to pass silt—causing the Wen to carry sand into the transport route and daily silting to grow higher.
