translations.idiomatic: Grain Director Su Fengwen said: "North of Anshan, the canal relies entirely on divided Wen River water, and only above Linqing does it begin to receive the help of Wei water.

sentences.zh: 今黃河橫亙於中，挾汶東下，安山以北毫無來源，應於衛河入運及張秋清黃相接處，各建一閘，蓄高衛水，使之南行，俟漕船過齊，即啟臨清新閘，仍放衛北流，以資浮送。

translations.literal: Now the Yellow River lies across the middle, carrying Wen River east downward; north of Anshan there is no source at all; at the place where the Wei River enters the transport canal and where Zhangqiu clear and Yellow meet, a lock should be built at each, storing high Wei River water and making it flow south; when grain ships have passed Qi, then open the new Linqing lock and again release the Wei northward to aid floating transport.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Yellow River lies across the middle and carries the Wen eastward, leaving north of Anshan with no source at all. A lock should be built where the Wei River enters the canal and another where clear and Yellow waters meet at Zhangqiu, storing Wei water high and making it travel south; after the grain boats have passed through Shandong, open the new Linqing lock and release the Wei northward again to help float them.

sentences.zh: 並於張秋淤高處挑深丈餘，安山以南亦一律挑濬，庶黃水未漲以前，運河既深，舟行自易。」

translations.literal: Also at Zhangqiu's high-silt places dredge more than a zhang deep; south of Anshan likewise dredge throughout—in hope that before Yellow River water has not yet risen, the Grand Canal will already be deep and boat travel naturally easy."
translations.idiomatic: Also dredge the high silted places at Zhangqiu more than a zhang deep, and dredge everything south of Anshan uniformly, so that before the Yellow River water rises, the canal will already be deep and boats can travel easily."

sentences.zh: 江督曾國籓言：「河運處處艱阻，如嶧縣大泛口沙淤停積，水深不及二尺，必須挑深四五尺，並將近灘石堆劃除，與河底配平，方利行駛。

translations.literal: Jiangsu Governor Zeng Guofan said: "River transport is everywhere hard and obstructed; for example at Yixian Dafankou sand silt stops and accumulates, water depth not reaching two chi—one must dredge four or five chi deep, and also cut away stone heaps near the banks, leveling with the river bottom, before travel is benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu Governor Zeng Guofan said: "River transport is difficult and obstructed everywhere. For example, at Dafankou in Yixian, sand and silt have accumulated until the water is less than two chi deep; it must be dredged four or five chi deeper, and the stone piles near the shoal must be cleared away and leveled with the riverbed before travel will be easy.

sentences.zh: 北則滕縣郗山口入湖要道，淺而且窄，微山湖之王家樓、滿家口、安家口，獨山湖之利建閘，南陽湖北之新店閘、華家淺、石佛閘，南旺閘分水龍王廟北之劉老口、袁口閘，處處淤淺，或數十丈至百餘丈，須一律挑深。

translations.literal: To the north, Teng County's Xishankou is the vital route entering the lake, shallow and moreover narrow; at Weishan Lake's Wangjialou, Manjiakou, and Anjiakou, Dushan Lake's Lijian Lock, north of Nanyang Lake's Xindian Lock, Huajia Shoal, Shifo Lock, south of Nanwang Lock at the Water-Dividing Dragon King Temple's Liulaokou and Yuankou locks—everywhere silted shallow, in places several tens of zhang to more than a hundred zhang, all must be dredged deep throughout.
translations.idiomatic: To the north, the key route into the lake at Xishankou in Teng county is both shallow and narrow; Wangjialou, Manjiakou, and Anjiakou on Weishan Lake; Lijian Lock on Dushan Lake; Xindian Lock, Huajia Shoal, and Shifo Lock north of Nanyang Lake; and Liulaokou and Yuankou Lock north of the water-dividing Dragon King Temple at Nanwang Lock are all silted and shallow, in places for several tens to more than a hundred zhang, and must all be dredged deep uniformly.

sentences.zh: 此未渡黃以前，阻滯之宜預為籌辦者。

translations.literal: These are obstructions before crossing the Yellow River that ought to be planned and handled in advance.
translations.idiomatic: These are the obstructions before crossing the Yellow River that should be planned for in advance.

sentences.zh: 至黃水穿運處，漸徙而南，自安山至八里廟五十五里運堤，盡被黃水沖壞，而十里鋪、姜家莊、道人橋均極淤淺，宜一面疏濬，一面於缺口排釘木椿，貫以巨索，俾船過有所依傍牽挽。

translations.literal: As for where Yellow River water pierces the transport canal, gradually shifting southward, from Anshan to Bali Temple for fifty-five li of transport dike, all was washed and destroyed by Yellow River water; and Shilipu, Jiangjiazhuang, and Daoren Bridge are all extremely silted shallow—one should dredge on one side, and on the other at gap openings drive and nail wooden piles in rows, strung with great ropes, so boats passing have something to lean on for towing.
translations.idiomatic: As for the place where Yellow River water cuts through the canal, it has gradually shifted south; the fifty-five li of canal dike from Anshan to Bali Temple have all been destroyed by Yellow River water, while Shilipu, Jiangjiazhuang, and Daoren Bridge are all extremely silted and shallow. It is proper to dredge on the one hand and, on the other, drive rows of wooden piles at the breaches and run heavy ropes through them so boats passing through have something to rely on for towing.

sentences.zh: 此渡黃時運道艱滯，宜預為籌辦者。

translations.literal: These are the transport route's hardships and delays when crossing the Yellow River that ought to be planned and handled in advance.
translations.idiomatic: These are the works that should be planned for in advance because the transport route is difficult and sluggish when crossing the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 渡黃以後，自張秋至臨河二百餘里，河身有高下，須開挖相等，於黃漲未落時，閉閘蓄水，以免消耗，或就平水南閘迤東築挑壩，引黃入運。

translations.literal: After crossing the Yellow River, from Zhangqiu to Linqing for more than two hundred li, the channel bed has highs and lows; one must excavate to make them equal. While the Yellow River flood has not yet subsided, close the locks and store water to avoid loss, or east of the Pingshui South Lock build spur dikes to draw Yellow River water into the transport canal.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Yellow River, the more than two hundred li from Zhangqiu to Linhe have high and low places in the river channel; they must be opened and dug to an even level. While the Yellow River flood has not yet fallen, close the locks and store water to avoid loss, or build a training dam east of the Pingshui South Lock to draw the Yellow River into the canal.

sentences.zh: 此渡黃後運道易涸，宜預為籌辦者。

translations.literal: These are matters that ought to be planned and handled in advance because after crossing the Yellow River the transport route easily dries up.
translations.idiomatic: These are the works that should be planned for in advance because the transport route easily dries after crossing the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 東平運河之西有鹽河，為東省鹽船經行要道。

translations.literal: West of the Dongping section of the transport canal is the Salt River, the main route along which Shandong salt boats travel.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Dongping canal is the Salt River, the main route used by Shandong salt boats.

sentences.zh: 若漕船由安山左近入鹽河，至八里廟仍歸運道，計程百餘里，較之徑渡黃流，上有缺口大溜，下有亂石樹舂者，難易懸殊。

translations.literal: If grain boats from near Anshan enter the Salt River and at Bali Temple still return to the transport route, the distance reckoned at more than a hundred li—compared with directly crossing the Yellow River current, above having gap openings and great flow, below having jumbled stones and tree pounders—the difference in difficulty would be extreme.
translations.idiomatic: If grain boats enter the Salt River near Anshan and return to the transport route at Bali Temple, the distance is somewhat more than a hundred li; compared with crossing the Yellow River current directly, where there are gap breaches and a great current above and jumbled stones and tree stumps below, the difference in difficulty is vast.

sentences.zh: 如行抵安山，遇黃流過猛，宜變通改道，須先勘明立標為志。

translations.literal: If upon reaching Anshan one meets Yellow River flow too fierce, a flexible change of route is appropriate; one must first survey clearly and set markers as guides.
translations.idiomatic: If, when the boats reach Anshan, the Yellow River current is too fierce, it would be proper to adapt by changing routes, but the route must first be surveyed clearly and markers set up.

sentences.zh: 此又渡黃改道，宜預為籌辦者。」

translations.literal: This is again a matter of changing route after crossing the Yellow River that ought to be planned and handled in advance."
translations.idiomatic: This is another alternate route after crossing the Yellow River that should be planned for in advance."

sentences.zh: 下河、漕督及東撫商籌。

translations.literal: The Lower River officials, the Grain Transport commissioner, and the Shandong governor deliberated together.
translations.idiomatic: The Lower River office, the grain transport commissioner, and the Shandong governor then held joint consultations.

sentences.zh: 十一年，河督喬松年請在張秋立閘，借黃濟運。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, River Commissioner Qiao Songnian requested establishing a lock at Zhangqiu to borrow Yellow River water to aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi, River Commissioner Qiao Songnian proposed a lock at Zhangqiu to feed the canal with Yellow River water.

sentences.zh: 同知蔣作錦則議導衛濟運。

translations.literal: Sub-Prefect Jiang Zuojin, on the other hand, proposed diverting the Wei River to aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: Sub-Prefect Jiang Zuojin urged diverting the Wei River instead.

sentences.zh: 上詢之直督李鴻章，鴻章言：「當年清口淤墊，即借黃濟運之病。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired of Zhili Governor Li Hongzhang; Hongzhang said: "In those years when Qingkou silted and filled, it was precisely the disease of borrowing Yellow River water to aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Zhili Governor Li Hongzhang about it, and Li Hongzhang said: "The silting at Qingkou in those years was precisely the harm caused by using Yellow River water to support transport.

sentences.zh: 今張秋河寬僅數丈，若引重濁之黃以閘壩節宣用之，水勢抬高，其淤倍速。

translations.literal: Now at Zhangqiu the river is only several zhang wide; if one draws heavy muddy Yellow River water and uses locks and dams to regulate and apply it, the water level rises and silting doubles in speed.
translations.idiomatic: Now the river at Zhangqiu is only several zhang wide. If heavy, muddy Yellow River water is drawn in and regulated by locks and dams, the water level will be raised and the silting will be twice as fast.

sentences.zh: 至作錦導衛，原因張秋北無清水灌運，故為此議。

translations.literal: As for Zuojin diverting the Wei, the reason was that north of Zhangqiu there is no clear water to irrigate the transport route, hence this proposal.
translations.idiomatic: As for Jiang Zuojin's proposal to divert the Wei, it arose because north of Zhangqiu there is no clear water to supply the transport route.

sentences.zh: 以全淮之強，不能敵黃，尚致倒灌停淤，豈一清淺之衛，遂能御黃濟運耶？

translations.literal: With the full strength of the Huai unable to resist the Yellow River, still causing backflow and stopped silt—how could one clear shallow Wei River then resist Yellow and aid transport?
translations.idiomatic: If the strength of the entire Huai cannot resist the Yellow River and still suffers backflow and silt stoppage, how could the clear and shallow Wei alone resist the Yellow River and support transport?

sentences.zh: 其意蓋襲取山東諸水濟運之法。

translations.literal: His idea generally copied the method by which Shandong's various waters aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: His idea simply borrows the Shandong method of using various waters to support transport.

sentences.zh: 不知泰山之陽，水皆西流，因勢利導，百八十泉之水，源旺派多，自足濟運。

translations.literal: He did not know that south of Mount Tai all waters flow west; following the trend to guide them, the water of one hundred eighty springs—sources flourishing with many branches—is sufficient to aid transport.
translations.idiomatic: He does not understand that south of Mount Tai the waters all flow west; by guiding them according to the terrain, the water of one hundred eighty springs, with abundant sources and many branches, is itself sufficient to support transport.

sentences.zh: 衛水微弱，北流最順，今必屈曲使之南行，一水兩分，勢多不便。

translations.literal: Wei River water is weak; northward flow is most natural; now one must bend it to go south; one water split two ways—in many respects inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei water is weak, and its most natural course is northward. If it must now be bent south, one stream will be divided in two and the circumstances will be inconvenient in many ways.

sentences.zh: 若分沁入衛以助其源，沁水猛濁，一發難收，昔人已有明戒。

translations.literal: If one divides Qin River into Wei to aid its source, Qin water is fierce and muddy; once released it is hard to recover—former people already had clear warnings.
translations.idiomatic: If the Qin is divided into the Wei to assist its source, Qin water is fierce and muddy; once released, it is hard to restrain. Men of old already gave clear warnings about this.

sentences.zh: 近世治河兼言利運，遂致兩難，卒無長策。

translations.literal: In recent times river control also spoke of benefiting transport, thus leading to difficulty on both sides, ultimately with no long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times river management has also spoken of benefiting transport, and this has led to two difficulties, with ultimately no lasting plan.

sentences.zh: 事窮則變，變則通。

translations.literal: When affairs reach extremity then change; change then succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: When an affair reaches exhaustion, it changes; when it changes, it opens a way through.

sentences.zh: 今沿海數千里，洋舶駢集，為千古以來創局，正不妨借海道轉輸，由滬解津，較為便速。」

translations.literal: Now along the coast for several thousand li foreign ships gather thick—a situation unprecedented since antiquity; just so, it is not inappropriate to borrow the sea route for transport, from Shanghai to discharge at Tianjin—more convenient and swift."
translations.idiomatic: Now foreign ships crowd the coast for several thousand li, an unprecedented situation from ancient times to the present. There is no harm in using the sea route for shipment; sending it from Shanghai to Tianjin is comparatively convenient and fast."

sentences.zh: 疏入，詔江、安糧道漕米年約十萬石仍由河運，餘仍由海運。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; an edict said Jiangsu and Anhui grain-route tribute grain, about one hundred thousand shi yearly, still by river transport; the remainder still by sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received, and the court ordered that roughly one hundred thousand shi of Jiangsu and Anhui tribute grain each year would still travel by canal while the rest continued by sea.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，東撫李元華條上運河上中下三等辦法，並言量東省財力，擬用中等，將北運河一律疏通，復還舊址，並建筑北閘。

translations.literal: Guangxu year three, Shandong Governor Li Yuanhua memorialized itemizing upper, middle, and lower three grades of methods for the canal, also saying that measuring Shandong's financial strength, he intended to use the middle grade, dredge the northern canal throughout, restore old sites, and build the north lock.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3, Shandong Governor Li Yuanhua submitted three graded plans for the canal and, gauging provincial finances, proposed the middle option: dredge the northern canal throughout, restore its old alignment, and rebuild the north lock.

sentences.zh: 時值年荒，寓賑於工，省而又省，需費三十萬有奇。

translations.literal: At the time of famine year, combining relief in the works, economizing again and again, requiring funds of more than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With famine abroad he folded relief into the project and pared costs repeatedly, yet the work would still need somewhat more than three hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 下所司議。

translations.literal: It was referred to the relevant offices for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was sent down for departmental review.

sentences.zh: 五年，有請復河運者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, some petitioned to restore river transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Guangxu, memorials appeared urging a return to canal transport.

sentences.zh: 江督沈葆楨言：「以大勢言之，前人之於河運，皆萬不得已而後出此者也。

translations.literal: Jiangsu Governor Shen Baozhen said: "Speaking of the great trend, former people's river transport was all a last resort after nothing else would do.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu Governor Shen Baozhen said: "Speaking of the general situation, earlier men resorted to river transport only when they had no other choice.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐都長安，宋都汴梁，舍河運無他策。

translations.literal: Han and Tang had their capitals at Chang'an, Song at Bianliang—apart from river transport there was no other policy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han and Tang made their capitals at Chang'an and the Song at Bianliang, there was no plan other than river transport.

sentences.zh: 然屢經險阻，官民交困，卒以中道建倉，伺便轉餽，而後疏失差少。

translations.literal: Yet repeatedly meeting peril, officials and people both strained; finally building granaries mid-route and waiting for convenience to relay grain—and only then were losses somewhat fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after repeated dangers and obstructions, officials and people were both exhausted; only when granaries were built midway and grain was relayed when convenient did failures become somewhat fewer.

sentences.zh: 元則專行海運，故終元世無河患。

translations.literal: Yuan then exclusively used sea transport, so through the Yuan era there were no river calamities.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan used sea transport alone, and therefore through the whole Yuan dynasty there were no river disasters.

sentences.zh: 有明而後，汲汲於河運。

translations.literal: From Ming onward, eagerly pursuing river transport.
translations.idiomatic: From the Ming onward, the state was urgent about river transport.

sentences.zh: 遂不得不致力於河防。

translations.literal: Thus there was no choice but to devote effort to river defense.
translations.idiomatic: It therefore had no choice but to devote effort to river defense.

sentences.zh: 運甫定章，河忽改道。

translations.literal: Transport rules were just settled when the river suddenly changed course.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the transport regulations were fixed, the river suddenly changed course.

sentences.zh: 河流不時遷徙，漕政與為轉移，我朝因之。

translations.literal: River flows constantly shift; grain transport policy shifts with them; our dynasty followed this.
translations.idiomatic: As the river flow shifted from time to time, grain policy shifted with it, and our dynasty followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 前督臣創為海運之說，漕政於窮無復之之時，藉以維持不敝。

translations.literal: Former governors created the sea-transport proposal; grain administration at a hopeless dead end relied on it to maintain without collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Former governors created the proposal for sea transport; when grain policy had reached an impasse with no way to restore it, this was used to maintain it without collapse.

sentences.zh: 議者謂運河貫通南北，漕艘藉資轉達，兼以保衛民田，意謂運道存則水利亦存，運道廢則水利亦廢。

translations.literal: Discussants said the transport canal runs through north and south, grain boats rely on it for conveyance, and also to protect farmland—meaning if the transport route exists then water works exist; if the transport route is abolished then water works are abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Some discussants say that the canal runs through north and south, that grain boats rely on it for transport, and that it also protects the people's fields. Their idea is that if the transport route survives, water control survives too; if the transport route is abandoned, water control is abandoned too.

sentences.zh: 臣以為舍運道而言水利易，兼運道而籌水利難。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks: apart from the transport route, speaking of water works is easy; including the transport route and planning water works is hard.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that speaking of water control while setting aside the transport route is easy; planning water control while also serving the transport route is hard.

sentences.zh: 民田於運道勢不兩立。

translations.literal: Farmland and the transport route cannot coexist in power.
translations.idiomatic: The people's fields and the transport route are fundamentally incompatible.

sentences.zh: 兼旬不雨，民欲啟涵洞以溉田，官必閉涵洞以養船。

translations.literal: For half a month without rain, the people want to open culverts to irrigate fields; officials must close culverts to nourish boats.
translations.idiomatic: After two ten-day periods without rain, the people want to open culverts to irrigate their fields, while officials must close the culverts to nurture the boats.

sentences.zh: 迨運河水溢，官又開閘壩以保堤，堤下民田立成巨浸，農事益不可問。

translations.literal: When transport canal water overflows, officials again open locks and dams to protect the dike; farmland below the dike immediately becomes a vast flood; farming becomes increasingly beyond inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When the canal water overflows, officials again open locks and dams to protect the dikes, and the people's fields below the dikes immediately become vast inundations; agriculture becomes still less manageable.

sentences.zh: 議者又太息經費之無措，舳艫之不備，以致河運無成。

translations.literal: Discussants again deeply sighed that funds could not be raised and ships were not prepared, causing river transport to fail.
translations.idiomatic: Others again sigh that funds cannot be found and vessels are not prepared, causing river transport to fail.

sentences.zh: 臣以為即使道光間歲修之銀與官造之船，至今一一俱存，以行漕於借黃濟運之河，未見其可也。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks that even if Daoguang-era annual repair silver and government-built ships all still existed today one by one, to run grain transport on a river that borrows Yellow River water to aid transport—one sees no feasibility.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that even if the annual-repair silver and government-built boats from the Daoguang years all survived intact today, I still do not see that they could carry grain on a river that uses Yellow River water to support transport.

sentences.zh: 近年江北所雇船隻，不及從前糧艘之半，然必俟黃流汛漲，竭千百勇夫之力以挽之，過數十船而淤復積。

translations.literal: In recent years boats hired in northern Jiangsu are not half the former grain fleet; yet one must wait for Yellow River flood season, exhaust the strength of thousands of stalwart laborers to tow them, and after several tens of boats silt accumulates again.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, the hired boats north of the Yangtze are not even half the former grain fleet, yet they must wait for the Yellow River's flood rise and exhaust the strength of thousands of brave men to tow them; after several tens of boats have passed, silt again accumulates.

sentences.zh: 今日所淤，必甚於去日，而今朝所費，無益於明朝。

translations.literal: Today's silting must exceed yesterday's, and today's spending benefits not tomorrow's court.
translations.idiomatic: What silts today must be worse than what silted yesterday, and what is spent this morning is of no benefit tomorrow morning.

sentences.zh: 即使船大且多，何所施其技乎？

translations.literal: Even if boats were large and many, where would their skill be applied?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the boats were large and numerous, where could their skill be applied?

sentences.zh: 近因西北連年亢旱，黃河來源不旺，遂乃狎而玩之。

translations.literal: Recently because the northwest had drought years on end, Yellow River sources were not strong—thus people treated it lightly and disdained it.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because the northwest has had successive years of severe drought and the Yellow River's sources are not abundant, people have grown familiar with it and treated it lightly.

sentences.zh: 物極必返，設因濟運而奪溜，北趨則畿輔受其害，南趨則淮、徐受其害，如民生何？

translations.literal: Things at extremity must return; suppose for aiding transport one seizes the current—if it trends north then the capital region suffers harm, if south then Huai and Xu suffer harm—what of the people's livelihood?
translations.idiomatic: When things reach an extreme they must reverse. If, in order to support transport, the current were seized and made to run north, the capital region would suffer; if it ran south, Huai and Xu would suffer. What would become of the people's livelihood?

sentences.zh: 如國計何？」

translations.literal: What of state finances?"
translations.idiomatic: What would become of the state's finances?"

translations.literal: He closed his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He closed his memorial.

sentences.zh: 八年，伏秋大汛，張家灣運河自蘇庄至姚辛庄沖開新河一段，長七百餘丈，上下口均與舊河接，形勢順直，大溜循之而下。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, summer-autumn great flood, the Zhangjiawan canal from Suzhuang to Yaoxinzhuang was breached open into a new river section, length more than seven hundred zhang; upper and lower mouths both joined the old river; formation straight; the main current followed it downward.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year a summer flood cut a new seven-hundred-zhang channel through the Zhangjiawan canal from Suzhuang to Yaoxinzhuang, both ends tying into the old bed along a straight line that carried the main current.

sentences.zh: 舊河上口至下口，長六千四百餘丈，業已斷流，惟新河身系自行沖開，不能一律深通。

translations.literal: The old river from upper mouth to lower mouth, length more than six thousand four hundred zhang, already had cut-off flow; only the new channel was self-breached and could not be uniformly deep and clear throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The old six-thousand-four-hundred-zhang reach above and below lay dry, while the new cut, opened by the flood itself, was not uniformly deep.

sentences.zh: 明年，直督李鴻章飭制新式鐵口刮泥大板，在兩岸拖拉，使一律通暢。

translations.literal: The next year, Zhili Governor Li Hongzhang ordered manufacture of new-style iron-mouth mud-scraping great boards, towed on both banks, to make passage uniformly smooth.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhili Governor Li Hongzhang had new iron-mouthed mud-scrapers built and hauled along both banks until the channel ran clear throughout.

sentences.zh: 十二年，通州潮白河之平家甿漫口，東趨入箭桿河。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, at Tongzhou on the Chaobai River at Pingjiatun there was an overflow breach, trending east into the Jian'gan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Chaobai River broke through at Pingjiatun near Tongzhou and poured east into the Jian'gan River.

sentences.zh: 未幾，堵復運河故道。

translations.literal: Before long, it was blocked and the canal's old route restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the breach was closed and the canal's old course restored.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，復漫刷平家甿新工下之北市庄東小堤，並老堤續塌百數十丈，連成一口，奪溜東趨十之八。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, sixth month, again overflow scoured the small dike east of Beishizhuang below Pingjiatun's new work, and the old dike continued to collapse for more than a hundred zhang, joining into one breach, seizing eight-tenths of the current eastward.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year flood again scoured the small levee east of Beishizhuang below the Pingjiatun repair; the old levee collapsed for another hundred-odd zhang into one gap that carried eight-tenths of the flow east.

sentences.zh: 尋堵塞之。

translations.literal: Soon it was blocked up.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon closed again.

sentences.zh: 是年，河決鄭州，山東黃水斷流，漕船不能南下，向之借黃濟運者，至是束手無策。

translations.literal: That year, the river burst at Zhengzhou; Shandong Yellow River water cut off flow; grain boats could not go south; those who formerly borrowed Yellow River water to aid transport—at this point were helpless with no plan.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Yellow River broke at Zhengzhou and its Shandong reach ran dry; grain boats could not move south, and advocates of borrowing the river for transport were left without recourse.

sentences.zh: 旋將臨口積淤疏挑，空船始得由黃入運。

translations.literal: Soon accumulated silt at Linqing mouth was dredged and excavated; only then could empty boats enter the transport canal from the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging then cleared the silt at Linqing mouth so empty boats could at last pass from the Yellow River into the canal.

sentences.zh: 十五年，東撫張曜言：「河運未能久停，請改海運漕米二十萬仍歸河運。」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Shandong Governor Zhang Yao said: "River transport cannot long be stopped; I request changing two hundred thousand shi of sea-transport tribute grain back to river transport."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Shandong Governor Zhang Yao said: "River transport cannot be suspended for long. Please change two hundred thousand shi of grain now sent by sea back to river transport."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十六年，用江督曾國荃言，修揚屬南運河堤閘涵洞，及附城附鎮塼工。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, following Jiangsu Governor Zeng Guoquan's advice, the south transport canal dikes, locks, and culverts in Yangzhou subordinates were repaired, and brick works adjoining cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, on the advice of Jiangsu Governor Zeng Guoquan, the southern canal levees, locks, and culverts in the Yangzhou region were repaired, along with brick revetments at towns and cities.

sentences.zh: 又用漕督松椿言，濬邳、宿運河。

translations.literal: Also following Grain Transport Commissioner Song Chun's advice, the Pi and Su canal sections were dredged.
translations.idiomatic: On the advice of Grain Transport Commissioner Song Chun, the canal through Pi and Su counties was dredged.

sentences.zh: 十九年，潮白河漲溢，運堤兩岸決口七十餘，上游務關廳決口七。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the Chaobai River rose and overflowed; on both banks of the transport dike more than seventy breaches; upstream at the Wuguan Office seven breaches.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Chaobai River flooded, opening more than seventy breaks along the canal levees and seven more at the upstream Wuguan office.

sentences.zh: 是冬均塞。

translations.literal: That winter all were blocked up.
translations.idiomatic: All were closed that winter.

sentences.zh: 二十年，濬濟寧、汶上、滕、嶧、茌平、陽穀、東平各屬運河。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the transport canal in Jining, Wenshang, Teng, Yi, Chiping, Yanggu, and Dongping subordinates was dredged.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the canal was dredged through Jining, Wenshang, Teng, Yi, Chiping, Yanggu, and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 明年，濬陶城埠至臨清運河二百餘里。

translations.literal: The next year, the transport canal from Taochengbu to Linqing for more than two hundred li was dredged.
translations.idiomatic: The following year more than two hundred li from Taochengbu to Linqing were cleared.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，侍讀學士瑞洵言南漕改折，有益無損，請每年提折價在津購米以實倉庾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Hanlin Reader Ruixun said converting southern grain transport to cash payment benefits without loss, and requested yearly drawing commutation price at Tianjin to buy rice to fill granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Hanlin Reader Ruixun urged commuting southern tribute grain to cash, arguing it would help rather than harm, and asked that commutation funds each year buy rice at Tianjin to fill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 御史秦夔揚亦言河漕勞費太甚，請停江北河運。

translations.literal: Censor Qin Kuiyang also said river grain transport's labor and expense were too great, and requested stopping northern Jiangsu river transport.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qin Kuiyang likewise argued that canal transport cost too much in labor and money and asked that northern Jiangsu river carriage be halted.

sentences.zh: 皆不許，仍飭認真疏濬，照常起運。

translations.literal: All were not permitted; still ordered earnest dredging and transport to start as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were denied; the court instead ordered thorough dredging and the usual sailing season.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，聯軍入京師，各倉被占踞，倉儲粒米無存，江北河運行至德州，改由陸路運送山、陝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, allied armies entered the capital; all granaries were occupied; stored grain none remained; northern Jiangsu river transport reached Dezhou, then changed to overland transport to Shanxi and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year allied troops entered Beijing, granaries were seized and emptied, and northern Jiangsu grain boats that had reached Dezhou had their cargoes sent overland to Shanxi and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，慶親王奕劻、大學士李鴻章言：「漕糧儲積，關於運務者半，因時制宜，請詔各省漕糧全改折色，其採買運解收放儲備各事，分飭漕臣倉臣籌辦。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang said: "Tribute grain storage—half concerns transport affairs; adapting to the times, I request an edict that all provinces' tribute grain be entirely converted to cash color; purchase, transport, delivery, receipt, storage, and reserve matters be separately ordered grain and granary officials to plan and handle."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang said: "Of tribute grain storage, half concerns transport affairs. In adapting to the times, please issue an edict changing all provincial tribute grain to cash commutation, while ordering grain transport and granary officials separately to plan purchase, transport, receipt, issue, and storage."

sentences.zh: 自是河運遂廢，而運河水利亦由各省分籌矣。

translations.literal: From then river transport was abandoned, and transport canal water works also came under each province's separate planning.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter canal transport was abandoned, and upkeep of the Grand Canal's water works was left to the provinces separately.
